  1900                              <1> 	;	18/05/2025
  1901                              <1> 	;      [AmbiguousFileName] bits will be set 
  1902                              <1> 	;	if DOT file name contains '?' or '*'
  1903                              <1> 	;	   bit 0,1 -> '?' (bit 1 -> extension)
  1904                              <1> 	;	   bit 2,3 -> '*' (bit 3 -> extension)

  1926                              <1> 	; 06/03/2016
  1927                              <1> 	; Directory entry name limit (11 bytes) check for
  1928                              <1> 	; 'rename_directory_entry' procedure.
  1929                              <1> 	; (EDI points to Directory Entry)
  1930                              <1> 	; (If the file name would not contain a dot
  1931                              <1> 	; and file name length would be 12, this would cause to
  1932                              <1> 	; overwrite the attributes byte of the directory entry.)
  1933                              <1> 	;
  1934                              <1> 	mov	ch, 11 ; directory entry's name length

  2204                              <1> save_longname_sub_component:
  2205                              <1> 	; 19/07/2025
  2206                              <1> 	; 25/05/2025
  2207                              <1> 	; 20/05/2025 (TRDOS 386 v2.0.10)
  2208                              <1> 	;	-Major Modification-
  2209                              <1> 	; 13/02/2016
  2210                              <1> 	; 06/02/2016 (TRDOS 386 = TRDOS v2.0)
  2211                              <1> 	; 28/02/2010
  2212                              <1> 	; 17/10/2009
  2213                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
  2214                              <1> 	;	EDI = Directory Entry
  2215                              <1> 	;     	// This procedure is called
  2216                              <1> 	;	// from 'find_directory_entry' procedure.
  2217                              <1> 	;	// If the last entry returns with
  2218                              <1> 	;	// a non-zero LongnameFound value and
  2219                              <1> 	;	// if LFN_CheckSum value is equal to
  2220                              <1> 	;	// the next shortname checksum,
  2221                              <1> 	;	// long name is valid.
  2222                              <1> 	;	// If a longname is longer than 65 bytes,
  2223                              <1> 	;	// it is invalid for trdos. (>45h)
  2224                              <1> 	;
  2225                              <1> 	; 20/05/2025 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10
  2226                              <1> 	;	According to
  2227                              <1> 	;	Microsoft FAT32 File System Specification
  2228                              <1> 	;   ... Long names are limited to 255 chars,
  2229                              <1> 	;	(UCS-2, 2-byte character set)
  2230                              <1> 	;	not including the trailing NUL. ...
  2231                              <1> 	;   ... Total path length of can not exceed
  2232                              <1> 	;	260 chars including the trailing NUL. ...
  2233                              <1> 	;	(520 bytes)
  2234                              <1> 	;   So, in this version of TRDOS 386
  2235                              <1> 	;	UNICODE chars (two bytes) will be converted
  2236                              <1> 	;	to ASCII chars only using low bytes of
  2237                              <1> 	;	of two byte UNICODE chars,
  2238                              <1> 	;	as a very simple method.
  2239                              <1> 	;	(if the high byte is not zero,
  2240                              <1> 	;	 low byte will be returned as '_')
  2241                              <1> 	;
  2242                              <1> 	;	! 25/05/2025 !
  2243                              <1> 	;	TRDOS 386 v2.1 (v2.0.10) will use only
  2244                              <1> 	;	260 bytes (130 2-byte characters) buffer
  2245                              <1> 	;	for FAT LFN type long names. And TRDOS 386
  2246                              <1> 	;	kernel will ignore long file names if the
  2247                              <1> 	;	length is longer/more than 260 bytes.
  2248                              <1> 	;	(in other words: more than 10 LFN entries)
  2249                              <1> 	;	And the kernel will use unicode to ascii
  2250                              <1> 	;	conversion.. As result of the conversion,
  2251                              <1> 	;	ASCIIZ equivalent of the long name
  2252                              <1> 	;	will be returned with max. 128+NUL chars.
  2253                              <1> 	;	(260 byte limit -> LDIR_Ord byte,
  2254                              <1> 	;	"Last Long Entry" mark is 41h to 4Ah.)
  2255                              <1> 	;
  2256                              <1> 	;	(ASCIIZ name buffer size will be 129 bytes)
  2257                              <1> 	;	((unicode LFN buffer will be 260 bytes))
  2258                              <1> 	;
  2259                              <1> 	; Modified registers: NONE ; 19/07/2025 
  2260                              <1> 	;	ECX ; 20/05/2025
  2261                              <1> 	;
  2262                              <1> 
  2263 0000AE1D 57                  <1> 	push	edi
  2264 0000AE1E 56                  <1> 	push	esi
  2265                              <1> 	;push	ebx
  2266 0000AE1F 51                  <1> 	push	ecx ; 19/07/2025

  2770                              <1> 	; 24/06/2025

  2779                              <1> 	;	ESI = DOS short file name address

  2861                              <1> calculate_checksum:
  2862                              <1> 	; 20/05/2025 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10
  2863                              <1> 	;	-verified-
  2864                              <1> 	; 29/07/2022 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5)
  2865                              <1> 	; 13/02/2016 (TRDOS 386 = TRDOS v2.0)
  2866                              <1> 	; 17/10/2009 (DIR.ASM, 'proc_calculate_checksum')
  2867                              <1>         ;
  2868                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
  2869                              <1> 	;	ESI = 11 byte DOS File Name location
  2870                              <1> 	;	(in DOS Directory Entry Format)
  2871                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
  2872                              <1> 	;	 AL = 8 bit checksum (CRC) value
  2873                              <1> 	;
  2874                              <1> 	; (Modified registers: EAX, ECX, ESI)
  2875                              <1> 
  2876                              <1> 	; Erdogan Tan [ 17-10-2009 ]
  2877                              <1> 	;  'ror al, 1' instruction
  2878                              <1> 
  2879                              <1> 	; Erdogan Tan [ 20-06-2004 ]
  2880                              <1> 	; This 8086 assembly code is an original code
  2881                              <1> 	; which is adapted from C code in
  2882                              <1> 	; Microsoft FAT32 File System Specification
  2883                              <1> 	; Version 1.03, December 6, 2000
  2884                              <1> 	; Page 28
  2885                              <1> 
  2886 0000AFA9 30C0                <1> 	xor	al, al
  2887                              <1> 	;mov	ecx, 11
  2888                              <1> 	; 29/07/2022
  2889 0000AFAB 29C9                <1> 	sub	ecx, ecx
  2890 0000AFAD B10B                <1> 	mov	cl, 11
  2891                              <1> loc_next_sum:
  2892                              <1> 	;xor	ah, ah
  2893                              <1> 	;test	al, 1
  2894                              <1> 	;jz	short pass_ah_80h
  2895                              <1> 	;mov	ah, 80h
  2896                              <1> ;pass_ah_80h:
  2897                              <1> 	;shr	al, 1
  2898 0000AFAF D0C8                <1> 	ror	al, 1 ; 17/10/2009
  2899 0000AFB1 0206                <1> 	add	al, [esi]
  2900 0000AFB3 46                  <1> 	inc	esi
  2901                              <1> 	;add	al, ah

  2917                              <1> 	;	partially different than msdos/pcdos methods.

  3824                              <1> 	; 17/07/2010
  3825                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
  3826                              <1> 	; 	EDI = Directory Entry Address
  3827                              <1> 	;	ESI = Dot File Name Location
  3828                              <1> 	;	EAX = First Cluster
  3829                              <1> 	;	File Size = 0 (Must be set later)
  3830                              <1> 	;	CL = Attributes
  3831                              <1> 	;	CH = 0 (File size = 0)
  3832                              <1> 	;	(If CH>0, File size is in dword [EBX]) (*)
  3833                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
  3834                              <1> 	;	EDI = Directory Entry Address
  3835                              <1> 	;	ESI = Dot File Name Location (Capitalized)
  3836                              <1> 	;	If CH input = 0, File Size = 0
  3837                              <1> 	;	Otherwise file size is as dword [EBX] (*)
  3838                              <1> 	;	DX = Date, AX = Time in DOS Dir Entry format
  3839                              <1> 	;	EBX = same
  3840                              <1> 	;	ECX = same
  3841                              <1>

  3844                              <1> 	mov	[edi+11], cl ; Attributes
  3845                              <1> 	mov	[edi+26], ax ; FClusterLw, 26
  3846                              <1> 	shr	eax, 16
  3847                              <1> 	mov	[edi+20], ax ; FClusterHw, 20
  3848                              <1> 	;xor	ax, ax
  3849                              <1> 	; 29/07/2022
  3850                              <1> 	xor	eax, eax
  3851                              <1> 	mov	[edi+12], ax ; NTReserved, 12
  3852                              <1> 			     ; CrtTimeTenth, 13
  3853                              <1> 	or	ch, ch
  3854                              <1> 	jz	short loc_make_direntry_set_filesize
  3855                              <1>

  4408                              <1> 	; 18/07/2025 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10
  4409                              <1> delete_longname:
  4410                              <1> 	; Delete long directory entries.
  4411                              <1> 	;
  4412                              <1> 	; Input:
  4413                              <1> 	;   eax = the last long directory entry index number
  4414                              <1> 	;	  (the 1st entry in the directory order)
  4415                              <1> 	;   ebx = 1st cluster of the directory
  4416                              <1> 	;   edx = LDRVT address
  4417                              <1> 	;
  4418                              <1> 	; Output:
  4419                              <1> 	;   eax = file/dir entry (found) index number
  4420                              <1> 	;   ebx = the 1st cluster of the directory
  4421                              <1> 	;   edx = Logical Dos Drive parameters Table
  4422                              <1> 	;   edi = directory entry (in the dir buff)
  4423                              <1> 	;   ecx = current (last) cluster of the dir
  4424                              <1> 	;   esi = [CurrentBuffer] = dir buffer header
  4425                              <1> 	;
  4426                              <1> 	;   If CF = 1 -> error code in EAX
  4427                              <1> 	;
  4428                              <1> 	; Modified registers:
  4429                              <1> 	;	eax, ebx, ecx, esi, edi, ebp
  4430                              <1> 
  4431 0000B3D5 891D[FC9C0100]      <1> 	mov	[DIR_FCluster], ebx
  4432 0000B3DB A3[E39B0100]        <1> 	mov	[DirEntry_Counter], eax
  4433                              <1> 
  4434 0000B3E0 E8B1120000          <1> 	call	get_direntry_@
  4435 0000B3E5 721B                <1> 	jc	short dln_fail
  4436                              <1> 
  4437                              <1> 	;mov	eax, ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND ; 12
  4438 0000B3E7 B802000000          <1> 	mov	eax, ERR_NOT_FOUND ; 2
  4439 0000B3EC 807F0B0F            <1> 	cmp	byte [edi+dir_entry.dir_attr], 0Fh
  4440 0000B3F0 750F                <1> 	jne	short dln_fail_stc
  4441 0000B3F2 803F41              <1> 	cmp	byte [edi], 41h
  4442 0000B3F5 720B                <1> 	jb	short dln_fail
  4443                              <1> 	; this may not be necessary !
  4444 0000B3F7 B805000000          <1> 	mov	eax, ERR_PERM_DENIED ; 11
  4445 0000B3FC 803F4A              <1> 	cmp	byte [edi], 4Ah
  4446 0000B3FF 7602                <1> 	jna	short dln_1
  4447                              <1> 
  4448                              <1> dln_fail_stc:

  4451 0000B402 C3                  <1> 	retn
  4452                              <1> dln_1:
  4453                              <1> 	; edi = directory entry
  4454                              <1> 	; esi = directory buffer header
  4455                              <1> 	; eax = directory entry offset (0-480)
  4456                              <1> 	; ecx = current (last) cluster

  4459                              <1> dln_2:

  4469                              <1> 	; if al = 01h or al = 41h it is the 1st LFN entry

  4472 0000B41D 240F                <1> 	and	al, 0Fh

  4518                              <1> locate_current_dir_entry:
  4519                              <1> 	; 30/07/2022
  4520                              <1> 	; 29/07/2022 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5)
  4521                              <1> 	; 16/10/2016
  4522                              <1> 	; 15/10/2016
  4523                              <1> 	; 23/03/2016
  4524                              <1> 	; 27/02/2016 (TRDOS 386 = TRDOS v2.0)
  4525                              <1> 	; 01/08/2011 (DIR.ASM, 'proc_locate_current_dir_entry')
  4526                              <1> 	; 07/03/2010
  4527                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
  4528                              <1> 	;	EAX = Directory Entry (Index) Number (< 65536)
  4529                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
  4530                              <1> 	;	EDI = Directory Entry Address
  4531                              <1> 	; 	EAX = Cluster Number of Directory Buffer
  4532                              <1> 	;	EBX = Directory Buffer Entry Offset
  4533                              <1> 	;	ECX = DirBuff Valid Data identifier (CL)
  4534                              <1> 	;   	If CF = 0 and CL = 2 then
  4535                              <1> 	;	   directory buffer modified and
  4536                              <1> 	;	   must be written to disk.
  4537                              <1> 	; 	If CF = 0  and CL = 1 then
  4538                              <1> 	;	   dir buffer has been written to disk, already.
  4539                              <1> 	;	CF = 1 -> Error code in EAX (AL)
  4540                              <1> 	;
  4541                              <1> 	; (Modified registers: EAX, EDX, ECX, EBX, EDI)
  4542                              <1> 
  4543                              <1> loc_locate_current_dir_entry:

  4563                              <1> loc_lcde_cdl_check:

  4591                              <1> 	mov	ebx, ecx
  4592                              <1> 	mov	ecx, edx
  4593                              <1> 	; 16/10/2016 (12h -> 12)

  4596                              <1> 
  4597                              <1> loc_lcde_calc_dirbuff_cluster_offset:
  4598                              <1> 	;mov	bl, [esi+LD_BPB+SecPerClust]
  4599                              <1> 	;xor	bh, bh
  4600                              <1> 	;mov	ax, [esi+LD_BPB+BytesPerSec]
  4601                              <1> 	;mul	bx
  4602                              <1>  	;;or	dx, dx ; If bytes per cluster > 32KB it is invalid
  4603                              <1> 	;; 29/07/2022
  4604                              <1> 	;or	dl, dl
  4605                              <1> 	;jnz	short loc_lcde_invalid_format
  4606                              <1> 	; 29/07/2022
  4607                              <1> 	xor	ebx, ebx
  4608                              <1> 	mov	bl, [esi+LD_BPB+SecPerClust]
  4609                              <1> 	mov	ax, [esi+LD_BPB+BytesPerSec]
  4610                              <1> 	mul	ebx
  4611                              <1> 	mov	ecx, eax
  4612                              <1> 	;mov	cx, ax ; BYTES PER CLUSTER

  4616                              <1> 	cmp	eax, 65535
  4617                              <1> 	ja	short loc_lcde_invalid_format

  5932                              <1> 	; 01/08/2010 - 18/05/2011
  5933                              <1> 	;
  5934                              <1> 	;   Command Interpreter phase 1 enter ->
  5935                              <1> 	;           AL = 1 -> Caller is command interpreter
  5936                              <1> 	;           AL = 2 -> The second call, re-enter/continue
  5937                              <1> 	;   Phase 1 -> Check source file
  5938                              <1> 	;              'found' is required
  5939                              <1> 	;   Phase 2 -> Check destination file,
  5940                              <1> 	;              save 'found' or 'not found' status
  5941                              <1> 	;              'permission denied' error will be return
  5942                              <1> 	;              if attributes have not for ordinary file
  5943                              <1> 	;              without readonly attribute
  5944                              <1> 	;   Command Interpreter phase 1 return ->
  5945                              <1> 	;              DH = Source file attributes
  5946                              <1> 	;              DL = Destination file found status
  5947                              <1> 	;              EAX = 0
  5948                              <1> 	;   Command Interpreter phase 2 enter ->
  5949                              <1> 	;              AL = 2 -> Continue from the last position
  5950                              <1> 	;              AH =
  5951                              <1> 	;   Phase 3 -> Load source file or use read/write cluster method
  5952                              <1> 	;   Phase 4 -> Create destination file if it is not found
  5953                              <1> 	;   Phase 5 -> Open destination file
  5954                              <1> 	;   Phase 6 -> Read from source and write to destination
  5955                              <1> 	;   Phase 7 -> Unload source file, if it is loaded at memory
  5956                              <1> 	;       cf = 1 causes to return before the phase 7
  5957                              <1> 	;              but loaded file will be unloaded
  5958                              <1> 	;	       (allocated memory block will be deallocated)
  5959                              <1> 	;
  5960                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
  5961                              <1> 	;	 ESI = Source File Pathname (Asciiz)
  5962                              <1> 	;        EDI = Destination File Pathname (Asciiz)
  5963                              <1> 	;        AL = 0 --> Interrupt (System call)
  5964                              <1> 	;        AL > 0 --> Command Interpreter (Question)
  5965                              <1> 	;        AL = 1 --> Question Phase
  5966                              <1> 	;        AL = 2 --> Progress Phase
  5967                              <1> 	;
  5968                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
  5969                              <1> 	;	cf = 0 -> OK ; (*)
  5970                              <1> 	;	EAX = Destination file first cluster
  5971                              <1> 	;
  5972                              <1> 	;	31/08/2024 - TRDOS v2.0.9 ; (*)

  5974                              <1> 	;          ;	        (incomplete copy)
  5975                              <1> 	;          ;CH > 0 if file is (full) loaded at memory

  8584                              <1> ; 28/05/2025 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10
  8585                              <1> ;----------------------------------------------------------
  8586                              <1> ; (Windows) FAT long file name (LFN) to DOS short file name
  8587                              <1> ; conversion
  8588                              <1> 
  8589                              <1> ; 26/05/2025
  8590                              <1> ; TRDOS 386 v2.0.10 - Long to short file name conversion
  8591                              <1> ;
  8592                              <1> ; REF:
  8593                              <1> ; Microsoft - Long Filename Specification
  8594                              <1> ; Version 0.5, December 4, 1992
  8595                              <1> ;
  8596                              <1> ; The following steps are used to form an 8.3 basis from a long name.
  8597                              <1> ;
  8598                              <1> ; 1. Remove all spaces. For example "My File" becomes "MyFile".
  8599                              <1> ;
  8600                              <1> ; 2. Initial periods, trailing periods, and extra periods prior to 
  8601                              <1> ;    the last embedded period are removed.
  8602                              <1> ;
  8603                              <1> ;    For example ".logon" becomes "logon", "junk.c.o" becomes "junkc.o",
  8604                              <1> ;    and "main." becomes "main".
  8605                              <1> ;
  8606                              <1> ; 3. Translate all illegal 8.3 characters into "_" (underscore).
  8607                              <1> ;    
  8608                              <1> ;    For example, "The[First]Folder" becomes "The_First_Folder".
  8609                              <1> ;
  8610                              <1> ; 4. If the name does not contain an extension then truncate it to 6 characters.
  8611                              <1> ;    If the names does contain an extension, then truncate the first part 
  8612                              <1> ;    to 6 characters and the extension to 3 characters.
  8613                              <1> ;
  8614                              <1> ;    For example, "I Am A Dingbat" becomes "IAmADi" and not "IAmADing.bat",
  8615                              <1> ;    and "Super Duper Editor.Exe" becomes "SuperD.Exe".
  8616                              <1> ;
  8617                              <1> ; 5. If the name does not contain an extension then a "~1" is appended to
  8618                              <1> ;    the name. If the name does contain an extension, then a "~1" is appended
  8619                              <1> ;    to the first part of the name, prior to the extension.
  8620                              <1> ;
  8621                              <1> ;    For example, "MyFile" becomes "MyFile~1, and "Junk.bat" becomes "Junk~1.bat".
  8622                              <1> ;
  8623                              <1> ;    This numeric value is always added to help reduce the conflicts
  8624                              <1> ;    in the 8.3 name space for automatic generated names.
  8625                              <1> ;
  8626                              <1> ; 6. This step is optional dependent on the name colliding with an existing file.
  8627                              <1> ;    To resolve collisions the decimal number, that was set to 1, is incremented
  8628                              <1> ;    until the name is unique. The number of characters needed to store the number
  8629                              <1> ;    will grow as necessary from 1 digit to 2 digits and so on.
  8630                              <1> ;    If the  length of the basis (ignoring the extension) plus the dash and number
  8631                              <1> ;    exceeds 8 characters then the length of the basis is shortened until
  8632                              <1> ;    the new name fits in 8 characters.
  8633                              <1> ;
  8634                              <1> ;    For example, if "FILENA~1.EXE" conflicts the next names tried are
  8635                              <1> ;    "FILENA~2.EXE", "FILENA~3.EXE", ..., "FILEN~10.EXE", "FILEN~11.EXE", etc
  8636                              <1> ;
  8637                              <1> ; 26/05/2025 - Erdogan Tan
  8638                              <1> ; Note: If the long name is the same as it's short name converted to lower case,
  8639                              <1> ;	Windows 7 sets DIR_NTRes (directory entry) byte to 08h.
  8640                              <1> ;       For example: The created file name "denemefn" is written into
  8641                              <1> ;	the directory as the short name "DENEMEFN" without the long name entry,
  8642                              <1> ;	but 'DIR_NTRes' byte (reserved and suggested -by microsoft-
  8643                              <1> ;	to set it as zero) is set to 08h.)
  8644                              <1> ; 	((DIR_NTRes byte is at offset 12 of a directory entry.))
  8645                              <1> 
  8646                              <1> convert_name_from_lfn:
  8647                              <1> 	; 17/06/2025
  8648                              <1> 	; 28/05/2025
  8649                              <1> 	; 27/05/2025
  8650                              <1> 	; 26/05/2025 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10

 10279                              <1> search_directory_entry:
 10280                              <1> 	; Search a valid directory entry with index number
 10281                              <1> 	;
 10282                              <1> 	; Input:
 10283                              <1> 	;   eax = entry index number (dir entry counter)

 10296                              <1> 	;

 10302                              <1>

 10311                              <1>

 10318                              <1>

 10749                              <1> 	; 20/05/2025 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10
 10750                              <1> 	; Singlix FS short name specific procedure
 10751                              <1> 	;
 10752                              <1> 	; INPUT:
 10753                              <1> 	;  eax = number (FDT/DDT number)
 10754                              <1> 	;  edi = [#], formal string address

 10756                              <1> 	; OUTPUT:
 10757                              <1> 	;  [.......] = max. 10 digits between '[' & ']'
 10758                              <1> 	;  ecx = formal string size including '[' & ']'
 10759                              <1> 	;
 10760                              <1> 	; Modified registers: eax, ecx, edx

 11598                              <1> search_fs_shortname:
 11599                              <1> 	; Search short file/dir name in current directory
 11600                              <1> 	; ! (singlix fs) !
 11601                              <1> 	;
 11602                              <1> 	; Input:
 11603                              <1> 	;   esi = ASCIIZ (dos 8.3 dot) file name address
 11604                              <1> 	;	  -In fact: Max. 12 bytes + NUL-
 11605                              <1> 	;    al = attributes (positive)
 11606                              <1> 	;	  dir entry attribs and AL must be > 0
 11607                              <1> 	;    ah = negative attributes
 11608                              <1> 	;	  dir entry attribs or AH must be 0
 11609                              <1> 	;
 11610                              <1> 	;;  [Current_Drv] = Logical Dos Drive Number
 11611                              <1> 	;   ebx = DDT number of the directory
 11612                              <1> 	;		which the name will be searched
 11613                              <1> 	;;;;[Current_Dir_FCluster] = DDT num of the dir
 11614                              <1> 	;		which the name will be searched
 11615                              <1> 	;	          = 0 -> root directory
 11616                              <1> 	;   24/06/2025
 11617                              <1> 	;   [Current_LDRVT] = Logical DOS Drv. D. Tbl. Addr.
 11618                              <1> 	;
 11619                              <1> 	; Output:
 11620                              <1> 	;   19/06/2025
 11621                              <1> 	;   eax = file size
 11622                              <1> 	;    bh = 5th byte of file size
 11623                              <1> 	;    bl = attributes (FDT.Attributes)
 11624                              <1> 	;
 11625                              <1> 	;   ecx = date & time in MSDOS Dir Entry format
 11626                              <1> 	;    lw = time (16 bits) -HHHHHMMMMMMSSSSS-
 11627                              <1> 	;    hw = date (16 bits) -YYYYYYYMMMMDDDDD-
 11628                              <1> 	;
 11629                              <1> 	;   edx = Logical Dos Drive parameters Table
 11630                              <1> 	;   esi = ASCIIZ file/directory name
 11631                              <1> 	;	 (Max. 12 bytes + NUL, capitalized)
 11632                              <1> 	;
 11633                              <1> 	;    (diff. than msdos: basis name may be 12 bytes)
 11634                              <1> 	;	((msdos basis name limit: 8 bytes))
 11635                              <1> 	;	(see: 'convert_name_from_trfs' procedure)
 11636                              <1> 	;
 11637                              <1> 	;   edi = FDT/DDT buffer address
 11638                              <1> 	;
 11639                              <1> 	;   If CF = 1 -> error code in EAX
 11640                              <1> 	;
 11641                              <1> 	; Modified registers:
 11642                              <1> 	;	eax, ebx, ecx, edx, esi, edi, ebp

 12177                              <1> get_fs_ddt:
 12178                              <1> get_fs_fdt:
 12179                              <1> 	; Get File/Directory Description Table
 12180                              <1> 	; by using FDT/DDT number in (current) directory
 12181                              <1> 	; ! (singlix fs) !
 12182                              <1> 	;
 12183                              <1> 	; Input:
 12184                              <1> 	;   eax = FDT/DDT number
 12185                              <1> 	;
 12186                              <1> 	;;  [Current_Drv] = Logical Dos Drive Number
 12187                              <1> 	;   ebx = DDT number of the directory
 12188                              <1> 	;	  which the FDT/DDT will be searched
 12189                              <1> 	;;;;[Current_Dir_FCluster] = DDT num of the dir
 12190                              <1> 	;	  which the FDT/DDT will be searched
 12191                              <1> 	;	          = 0 -> root directory
 12192                              <1> 	;   24/06/2025
 12193                              <1> 	;   [Current_LDRVT] = Logical DOS Drv. D. Tbl. Addr.
 12194                              <1> 	;
 12195                              <1> 	; Output:
 12196                              <1> 	;   19/06/2025
 12197                              <1> 	;   eax = file size
 12198                              <1> 	;    bh = 5th byte of file size
 12199                              <1> 	;    bl = attributes (FDT.Attributes)
 12200                              <1> 	;
 12201                              <1> 	;   ecx = date & time in MSDOS Dir Entry format
 12202                              <1> 	;    lw = time (16 bits) -HHHHHMMMMMMSSSSS-
 12203                              <1> 	;    hw = date (16 bits) -YYYYYYYMMMMDDDDD-
 12204                              <1> 	;
 12205                              <1> 	;   edx = Logical Dos Drive parameters Table
 12206                              <1> 	;   esi = ASCIIZ file/directory name
 12207                              <1> 	;	 (Max. 12 bytes + NUL, capitalized)
 12208                              <1> 	;
 12209                              <1> 	;    (diff. than msdos: basis name may be 12 bytes)
 12210                              <1> 	;	((msdos basis name limit: 8 bytes))
 12211                              <1> 	;	(see: 'convert_name_from_trfs' procedure)
 12212                              <1> 	;
 12213                              <1> 	;   edi = FDT/DDT address
 12214                              <1> 	;
 12215                              <1> 	;   If CF = 1 -> error code in EAX
 12216                              <1> 	;
 12217                              <1> 	; Modified registers:
 12218                              <1> 	;	eax, ebx, ecx, edx, esi, edi, ebp
 12219                              <1> 	;
 12220                              <1> 
 12221 0000CFDD 891D[D5AE0100]      <1> 	mov	[FS_Current_DDT], ebx ; [DIR_FCluster]
 12222 0000CFE3 A3[D9AE0100]        <1> 	mov	[FDT_Number], eax
 12223                              <1> 
 12224                              <1> 	;xor	edx, edx
 12225                              <1> 	;mov	dh, [Current_Drv]
 12226                              <1> 	;add	edx, Logical_DOSDisks
 12227                              <1> 	; 24/06/2025
 12228 0000CFE8 8B15[D79B0100]      <1> 	mov	edx, [Current_LDRVT]

 12366                              <1> 	;
 12367                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
 12368                              <1> 	;	ESI = ASCIIZ Directory String Address
 12369                              <1> 	;	AL = Current Directory Level

 12695                              <1> search_fs_longname:
 12696                              <1> 	; Search long file/dir name in current directory
 12697                              <1> 	; ! (singlix fs) !
 12698                              <1> 	;
 12699                              <1> 	; Input:
 12700                              <1> 	;   esi = ASCIIZ (or 64 bytes) file name to be
 12701                              <1> 	;	  searched in the (current) directory
 12702                              <1> 	;;  [Current_Drv] = Logical Dos Drive Number

 12710                              <1> 	;

 12727                              <1> 	;

 12729                              <1> 	;
 12730                              <1> 	;   If CF = 1 -> error code in EAX
 12731                              <1> 	;

 12733                              <1> 	;	eax, ebx, ecx, edx, esi, edi, ebp

   272                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
   273                              <1> 	;	ESI = Logical DOS Drive Description Table

  1731                              <1> 	; INPUT ->

  1738                              <1> 	;	EAX = Free Space in sectors

  1745                              <1> 	;			          sign due to r/w error

  3839                              <1> FLUSHBUFFERS:
  3840                              <1> 	; 14/07/2025
  3841                              <1> 	; 13/07/2025
  3842                              <1> 	; 29/04/2025
  3843                              <1> 	; (MSDOS -> FLUSHBUF) - Ref: Retro DOS v5 - ibmdos7.s
  3844                              <1> 	; Write out all dirty buffers for disk and flag them as clean
  3845                              <1> 	;
  3846                              <1> 	; INPUT:
  3847                              <1> 	;	AL = Physical drive/disk number
  3848                              <1> 	;	   = -1 for all drives

  3853                              <1> 	;

  3855                              <1> 	;

  3857                              <1> 	;	EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI

  3927                              <1> 	; 14/07/2025

  3929                              <1> 	; (MSDOS -> CHECKFLUSH) - Ref: Retro DOS v5 - ibmdos7.s
  3930                              <1> 	; Write out a buffer if it is dirty
  3931                              <1> 	;
  3932                              <1> 	; INPUT:
  3933                              <1> 	;	AL = Physical drive/disk number
  3934                              <1> 	;	   = -1 for all drives (do not check drive number)

  3958 0000D9E4 7411                <1> 	jz	short chk_flush_2	; Buffer not dirty, cf = 0
  3959                              <1> 
  3960 0000D9E6 FF7608              <1> 	push	dword [esi+BUFFINFO.buf_ID]
  3961 0000D9E9 E832FFFFFF          <1> 	call	BUFWRITE
  3962 0000D9EE 58                  <1> 	pop	eax

  3964                              <1>

  3966 0000D9F4 894608              <1> 	mov	[esi+BUFFINFO.buf_ID], eax

  4686                              <1> FINDENTRY:
  4687                              <1> 	; 02/06/2025
  4688                              <1> 	; 11/05/2025
  4689                              <1> 	; (MSDOS -> FINDENTRY) - Ref: Retro DOS v5 - ibmdos7.s
  4690                              <1> 	;
  4691                              <1> 	; Look for a directory entry
  4692                              <1> 	;	(find file name in disk directory)
  4693                              <1> 	;
  4694                              <1> 	; INPUT:
  4695                              <1> 	;	;;;[THISDPB] = Base of drive parameters (MSDOS)
  4696                              <1> 	;	EDX Points to Logical Dos Drive Description Table
  4697                              <1> 	;	[SECCLUSPOS] = 0
  4698                              <1> 	;	[DIRSEC] = Starting directory sector number (physical)
  4699                              <1> 	;	[CLUSNUM] = Next cluster of directory
  4700                              <1> 	;	[CLUSFAC] = Sectors per cluster
  4701                              <1> 	;	[NAME1] = Name to look for
  4702                              <1> 	;
  4703                              <1> 	; OUTPUT:
  4704                              <1> 	;	If cf = 1 -> name not found
  4705                              <1> 	;	if cf = 0
  4706                              <1> 	;		Zero set if attributes match
  4707                              <1> 	;			 (always except when creating)
  4708                              <1> 	;	;;;[THISDPB] = Base of drive parameters (MSDOS)
  4709                              <1> 	;	EDX Points to Logical Dos Drive Description Table
  4710                              <1> 	;	EBX = Pointer into directory buffer
  4711                              <1> 	;	ESI = Pointer to 1st Cluster field in directory entry
  4712                              <1> 	;	;[CURBUF] has directory record with match (MSDOS)
  4713                              <1> 	;	[CurrentBuffer] has directory sector with match
  4714                              <1> 	;	[NAME1] has file name
  4715                              <1> 	;	[LASTENT] is entry number of the entry
  4716                              <1> 	;
  4717                              <1> 	; Modified registers:
  4718                              <1> 	;	EAX, EBX, ECX, ESI, EDI, EBP
  4719                              <1> 	;
  4720                              <1>

  4723 0000DC7E 24DE                <1> 	and	al, ~attr_ignore	; Ignore useless bits
  4724 0000DC80 3C08                <1> 	cmp	al, attr_volume_id	; Looking for vol ID only ?
  4725 0000DC82 7505                <1> 	jne	short NotVolSrch	; No
  4726 0000DC84 E86AFBFFFF          <1> 	call	SETROOTSRCH		; Yes force search of root
  4727                              <1> NotVolSrch:

  4732                              <1> 	; ECX = Pointer to first byte after end of CURBUF
  4733                              <1> 	; [LASTENT] = New directory entry number
  4734                              <1> 	; [NXTCLUSNUM],[SECCLUSPOS] set
  4735                              <1> 	; EDX = LDRVT address (MSDOS -> [THISDPB])
  4736                              <1> SRCH:

  4738 0000DC90 C605[88AE0100]00    <1> 	mov	byte [LNE_COUNT], 0	; reset long name entry count

  4798                              <1> findentry_found:
  4799                              <1> 	; We have a file with a matching name.
  4800                              <1> 	; We must now consider the attributes:
  4801                              <1> 	
  4802                              <1> 	; ATTRIB     Action
  4803                              <1> 	; ------     ------

  4846                              <1> 	; (MSDOS -> STARTSRCH) - Ref: Retro DOS v5 - ibmdos7.s
  4847                              <1> 	;
  4848                              <1> 	; Initiate a directory search
  4849                              <1> 	;	(Set up a search for GETENTRY and NEXTENTRY)
  4850                              <1> 	;
  4851                              <1> 	; INPUT:
  4852                              <1> 	;	;;;[THISDPB] = Base of drive parameters (MSDOS)
  4853                              <1> 	;	;EDX Points to Logical Dos Drive Description Table
  4854                              <1> 	; OUTPUT:
  4855                              <1> 	;	;;;ES:BP = Drive parameters (MSDOS)
  4856                              <1> 	;	;EDX Points to Logical Dos Drive Description Table

  4858                              <1> 	;	Sets up LASTENT=VOLID=0, ENTFREE=ENTLAST=-1
  4859                              <1> 	;
  4860                              <1> 	; Modified registers:
  4861                              <1> 	;	EAX

  4863                              <1> 
  4864                              <1> 	;;;;les	bp, [THISDPB]
  4865                              <1>

  4867 0000DD54 A3[58AE0100]        <1> 	mov	[LASTENT], eax

  4869 0000DD5E 48                  <1> 	dec	eax ; -1
  4870 0000DD5F A3[80AE0100]        <1> 	mov	[ENTFREE], eax

  4879                              <1> GETENTRY:
  4880                              <1> 	; 11/05/2025
  4881                              <1> 	; (MSDOS -> GETENTRY) - Ref: Retro DOS v5 - ibmdos7.s
  4882                              <1> 	;
  4883                              <1> 	; Locates directory entry in preparation for search
  4884                              <1> 	; (GETENT provides entry for passing desired entry in EAX)
  4885                              <1> 	;
  4886                              <1> 	; INPUT:
  4887                              <1> 	;	[LASTENT] has directory entry
  4888                              <1> 	;	EDX Points to Logical Dos Drive Description Table
  4889                              <1> 	;	[DIRSEC],[CLUSNUM],[CLUSFAC],[ENTLAST] set
  4890                              <1> 	;					 for DIR involved
  4891                              <1> 	; OUTPUT:
  4892                              <1> 	;	EBX = Pointer to next directory entry in CURBUF
  4893                              <1> 	;	ECX = Pointer to first byte after end of CURBUF
  4894                              <1> 	;	[LASTENT] = New directory entry number
  4895                              <1> 	;	[NXTCLUSNUM],[SECCLUSPOS] set via DIRREAD

  5688                              <1> 	; set up a . or .. directory entry for a directory
  5689                              <1> 	;
  5690                              <1> 	; INPUT:

  5694                              <1> 	;			 in MSDOS directory entry format

  5697                              <1> 	;     edi = next directory entry position

    20                              <1> sysent: ; < enter to system call >
    21                              <1> 	; 15/07/2026 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.1.0
    22                              <1> 	; 01/05/2026 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.11
    23                              <1> 	; 08/01/2026 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.10 (v2.1.0)
    24                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5
    25                              <1> 	; 17/03/2017
    26                              <1> 	; 03/03/2017
    27                              <1> 	; 19/02/2017
    28                              <1> 	; 13/01/2017
    29                              <1> 	; 06/06/2016
    30                              <1> 	; 29/04/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
    31                              <1> 	; 16/04/2015 - 19/10/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1)
    32                              <1> 	; 10/04/2013 - 18/01/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
    33                              <1> 	;
    34                              <1> 	; 'unkni' or 'sysent' is sytem entry from various traps.
    35                              <1> 	; The trap type is determined and an indirect jump is made to
    36                              <1> 	; the appropriate system call handler. If there is a trap inside
    37                              <1> 	; the system a jump to panic is made. All user registers are saved
    38                              <1> 	; and u.sp points to the end of the users stack. The sys (trap)
    39                              <1> 	; instructor is decoded to get the the system code part (see
    40                              <1> 	; trap instruction in the PDP-11 handbook) and from this
    41                              <1> 	; the indirect jump address is calculated. If a bad system call is
    42                              <1> 	; made, i.e., the limits of the jump table are exceeded, 'badsys'
    43                              <1> 	; is called. If the call is legitimate control passes to the
    44                              <1> 	; appropriate system routine.
    45                              <1> 	;
    46                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
    47                              <1> 	;	Through a trap caused by any sys call outside the system.
    48                              <1> 	; Arguments:
    49                              <1> 	;	Arguments of particular system call.
    50                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
    51                              <1> 	;
    52                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification: 
    53                              <1> 	;       System call number is in EAX register.
    54                              <1> 	;
    55                              <1> 	;       Other parameters are in EDX, EBX, ECX, ESI, EDI, EBP
    56                              <1> 	;	registers depending of function details.
    57                              <1>   	;
    58                              <1> 	; 16/04/2015
    59 0000DFEC 368925[9CB00100]    <1>         mov     [ss:u.sp], esp ; Kernel stack points to return address

    63 0000DFF4 06                  <1> 	push	es
    64 0000DFF5 0FA0                <1> 	push	fs
    65 0000DFF7 0FA8                <1> 	push	gs
    66 0000DFF9 60                  <1> 	pushad  ; eax, ecx, edx, ebx, esp -before pushad-, ebp, esi, edi
    67                              <1> 	;
    68                              <1> 	; ESPACE = [ss:u.sp] - esp ; 4*12 = 48 ; 17/09/2015 ; 06/06/2016
    69                              <1> 	; 	(ESPACE is size of space in kernel stack
    70                              <1> 	;	for saving/restoring user registers.)

   286                              <1> sysemt: ; enable (or disable) multi tasking -time sharing-
   287                              <1> 	;
   288                              <1> 	; 08/08/2022
   289                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
   290                              <1> 	; 23/05/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
   291                              <1> 	; 14/05/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1)
   292                              <1> 	; 10/12/2013 - 20/04/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
   293                              <1> 	;
   294                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification:
   295                              <1> 	;	'Enable Multi Tasking'  system call instead
   296                              <1> 	;	of 'Emulator Trap' in original UNIX v1 for PDP-11.
   297                              <1> 	;
   298                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 feature only!
   299                              <1> 	;	Using purpose: Kernel will start without time-out
   300                              <1> 	;	(internal clock/timer) functionality.
   301                              <1> 	;	Then etc/init will enable clock/timer for
   302                              <1> 	;	multi tasking.
   303                              <1> 	;
   304                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
   305                              <1> 	;	BL = 0 -> disable multi tasking
   306                              <1> 	;	BL > 1 -> enable multi tasking (time sharing)
   307                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
   308                              <1> 	;	none
   309                              <1> 	;
   310                              <1> 	;  Note: Multi tasking is disabled during system
   311                              <1> 	;	 initialization, it must be enabled by using
   312                              <1> 	;	 this system call. (Otherwise, running proces 
   313                              <1> 	;	 will not be changed by another process within
   314                              <1> 	;	 run time sequence/schedule, if running process
   315                              <1> 	;	 will not 'release' itself. Only 'wakeup' procedure
   316                              <1> 	;	 for waiting processes and programmed timer events
   317                              <1> 	;	 for other processes can change running process
   318                              <1> 	;	 while multi tasking is disabled.) ** 23/05/2016 **

   377                              <1> sysret: ; < return from system call>
   378                              <1> 	; 28/08/2024 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.9
   379                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5
   380                              <1> 	; 01/03/2017
   381                              <1> 	; 28/02/2017
   382                              <1> 	; 29/04/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
   383                              <1> 	; 16/04/2015 - 10/09/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1)
   384                              <1> 	; 10/04/2013 - 23/02/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
   385                              <1> 	;
   386                              <1> 	; 'sysret' first checks to see if process is about to be
   387                              <1> 	; terminated (u.bsys). If it is, 'sysexit' is called.
   388                              <1> 	; If not, following happens:
   389                              <1> 	; 	1) The user's stack pointer is restored.
   390                              <1> 	;	2) r1=0 and 'iget' is called to see if last mentioned
   391                              <1> 	;	   i-node has been modified. If it has, it is written out
   392                              <1> 	;	   via 'ppoke'.
   393                              <1> 	;	3) If the super block has been modified, it is written out
   394                              <1> 	;	   via 'ppoke'.
   395                              <1> 	;	4) If the dismountable file system's super block has been
   396                              <1> 	;	   modified, it is written out to the specified device
   397                              <1> 	;	   via 'ppoke'.
   398                              <1> 	;	5) A check is made if user's time quantum (uquant) ran out
   399                              <1> 	;	   during his execution. If so, 'tswap' is called to give
   400                              <1> 	;	   another user a chance to run.
   401                              <1> 	;	6) 'sysret' now goes into 'sysrele'.
   402                              <1> 	;	    (See 'sysrele' for conclusion.)
   403                              <1> 	;
   404                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
   405                              <1> 	;	jump table or 'br sysret'

   690                              <1> sysexit: ; <terminate process>
   691                              <1> 	; 08/01/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10
   692                              <1> 	; 22/08/2024
   693                              <1> 	; 20/08/2024
   694                              <1> 	; 18/08/2024 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.9
   695                              <1> 	; 30/07/2022
   696                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
   697                              <1> 	; 14/11/2017
   698                              <1> 	; 27/05/2017
   699                              <1> 	; 10/04/2017
   700                              <1> 	; 26/02/2017 - 28/02/2017
   701                              <1> 	; 02/01/2017 - 23/01/2017
   702                              <1> 	; 06/06/2016 - 10/06/2016
   703                              <1> 	; 19/05/2016 - 23/05/2016
   704                              <1> 	; 29/04/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
   705                              <1> 	; 16/04/2015 - 01/09/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1)
   706                              <1> 	; 19/04/2013 - 14/02/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
   707                              <1> 	;
   708                              <1> 	; 'sysexit' terminates a process. First each file that
   709                              <1> 	; the process has opened is closed by 'flose'. The process
   710                              <1> 	; status is then set to unused. The 'p.pid' table is then
   711                              <1> 	; searched to find children of the dying process. If any of
   712                              <1> 	; children are zombies (died by not waited for), they are
   713                              <1> 	; set free. The 'p.pid' table is then searched to find the
   714                              <1> 	; dying process's parent. When the parent is found, it is
   715                              <1> 	; checked to see if it is free or it is a zombie. If it is
   716                              <1> 	; one of these, the dying process just dies. If it is waiting
   717                              <1> 	; for a child process to die, it notified that it doesn't
   718                              <1> 	; have to wait anymore by setting it's status from 2 to 1
   719                              <1> 	; (waiting to active). It is awakened and put on runq by
   720                              <1> 	; 'putlu'. The dying process enters a zombie state in which
   721                              <1> 	; it will never be run again but stays around until a 'wait'
   722                              <1> 	; is completed by it's parent process. If the parent is not
   723                              <1> 	; found, process just dies. This means 'swap' is called with
   724                              <1> 	; 'u.uno=0'. What this does is the 'wswap' is not called
   725                              <1> 	; to write out the process and 'rswap' reads the new process
   726                              <1> 	; over the one that dies..i.e., the dying process is 
   727                              <1> 	; overwritten and destroyed.
   728                              <1>  	;
   729                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
   730                              <1> 	;	sysexit or conditional branch.
   731                              <1> 	; Arguments:
   732                              <1> 	;	-
   733                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
   734                              <1> 	;
   735                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification: 
   736                              <1> 	;       System call number (=1) is in EAX register.
   737                              <1> 	;
   738                              <1> 	;       Other parameters are in EDX, EBX, ECX, ESI, EDI, EBP
   739                              <1> 	;       registers depending of function details.
   740                              <1> 	;
   741                              <1> 	; ('swap' procedure is mostly different than original UNIX v1.)
   742                              <1> 	;
   743                              <1> ; / terminate process
   744                              <1> 	; AX = 1
   745                              <1> 	;dec 	ax ; 0

  1040                              <1> syswait: ; < wait for a processs to die >
  1041                              <1> 	; 20/08/2024
  1042                              <1> 	; 30/07/2022
  1043                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
  1044                              <1> 	; 17/09/2015
  1045                              <1> 	; 02/09/2015
  1046                              <1> 	; 01/09/2015
  1047                              <1> 	; 16/04/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
  1048                              <1> 	; 24/05/2013 - 05/02/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
  1049                              <1> 	;
  1050                              <1> 	; 'syswait' waits for a process die.
  1051                              <1> 	; It works in following way:
  1052                              <1> 	;    1) From the parent process number, the parent's
  1053                              <1> 	; 	process name is found. The p.ppid table of parent
  1054                              <1> 	;	names is then searched for this process name.
  1055                              <1> 	;	If a match occurs, r2 contains child's process
  1056                              <1> 	;	number. The child status is checked to see if it is
  1057                              <1> 	;	a zombie, i.e; dead but not waited for (p.stat=3)
  1058                              <1> 	;	If it is, the child process is freed and it's name
  1059                              <1> 	;	is put in (u.r0). A return is then made via 'sysret'.
  1060                              <1> 	;	If the child is not a zombie, nothing happens and
  1061                              <1> 	;	the search goes on through the p.ppid table until
  1062                              <1> 	;	all processes are checked or a zombie is found.
  1063                              <1> 	;    2) If no zombies are found, a check is made to see if
  1064                              <1> 	;	there are any children at all. If there are none,
  1065                              <1> 	;	an error return is made. If there are, the parent's
  1066                              <1> 	;	status is set to 2 (waiting for child to die),
  1067                              <1> 	;	the parent is swapped out, and a branch to 'syswait'
  1068                              <1> 	;	is made to wait on the next process.
  1069                              <1> 	;
  1070                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
  1071                              <1> 	;	?
  1072                              <1> 	; Arguments:
  1073                              <1> 	;	-
  1074                              <1> 	; Inputs: -
  1075                              <1> 	; Outputs: if zombie found, it's name put in u.r0.
  1076                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
  1077                              <1> 	;
  1078                              <1> 
  1079                              <1> ; / wait for a process to die
  1080                              <1>

  1210                              <1> sysfork: ; < create a new process >
  1211                              <1> 	; 15/07/2026 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.1.0 
  1212                              <1> 	; 12/07/2026 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.11 (u.cdrv, u.cdir)
  1213                              <1> 	; 19/08/2024 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.9 (STDIN/STDOUT)
  1214                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5
  1215                              <1> 	; 02/01/2017 (TRDOS 386 modification)
  1216                              <1> 	; 04/09/2015 - 18/05/2015
  1217                              <1> 	; 28/08/2015 - 01/09/2015 - 02/09/2015
  1218                              <1> 	; 09/05/2015 - 10/05/2015 - 14/05/2015
  1219                              <1> 	; 06/05/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
  1220                              <1> 	; 24/05/2013 - 14/02/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
  1221                              <1> 	;
  1222                              <1> 	; 'sysfork' creates a new process. This process is referred
  1223                              <1> 	; to as the child process. This new process core image is
  1224                              <1> 	; a copy of that of the caller of 'sysfork'. The only
  1225                              <1> 	; distinction is the return location and the fact that (u.r0)
  1226                              <1> 	; in the old process (parent) contains the process id (p.pid)
  1227                              <1> 	; of the new process (child). This id is used by 'syswait'.
  1228                              <1> 	; 'sysfork' works in the following manner:
  1229                              <1> 	;    1) The process status table (p.stat) is searched to find
  1230                              <1> 	;	a process number that is unused. If none are found
  1231                              <1> 	;	an error occurs.
  1232                              <1> 	;    2) when one is found, it becomes the child process number
  1233                              <1> 	;	and it's status (p.stat) is set to active.
  1234                              <1> 	;    3) If the parent had a control tty, the interrupt
  1235                              <1> 	;	character in that tty buffer is cleared.
  1236                              <1> 	;    4) The child process is put on the lowest priority run
  1237                              <1> 	;	queue via 'putlu'.
  1238                              <1> 	;    5) A new process name is gotten from 'mpid' (actually
  1239                              <1> 	;	it is a unique number) and is put in the child's unique
  1240                              <1> 	;	identifier; process id (p.pid).
  1241                              <1> 	;    6) The process name of the parent is then obtained and
  1242                              <1> 	;	placed in the unique identifier of the parent process
  1243                              <1> 	;	name is then put in 'u.r0'.
  1244                              <1> 	;    7) The child process is then written out on disk by
  1245                              <1> 	;	'wswap',i.e., the parent process is copied onto disk
  1246                              <1> 	;	and the child is born. (The child process is written
  1247                              <1> 	;	out on disk/drum with 'u.uno' being the child process
  1248                              <1> 	;	number.)
  1249                              <1> 	;    8) The parent process number is then restored to 'u.uno'.
  1250                              <1> 	;    9) The child process name is put in 'u.r0'.
  1251                              <1> 	;   10) The pc on the stack sp + 18 is incremented by 2 to
  1252                              <1> 	;	create the return address for the parent process.
  1253                              <1> 	;   11) The 'u.fp' list as then searched to see what files
  1254                              <1> 	;	the parent has opened. For each file the parent has
  1255                              <1> 	;	opened, the corresponding 'fsp' entry must be updated
  1256                              <1> 	;	to indicate that the child process also has opened
  1257                              <1> 	;	the file. A branch to 'sysret' is then made.
  1258                              <1> 	;
  1259                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
  1260                              <1> 	;	from shell ?
  1261                              <1> 	; Arguments:
  1262                              <1> 	;	-
  1263                              <1> 	; Inputs: -
  1264                              <1> 	; Outputs: *u.r0 - child process name
  1265                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
  1266                              <1> 	;	
  1267                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification: 
  1268                              <1> 	;	AX = r0 = PID (>0) (at the return of 'sysfork')
  1269                              <1> 	;	= process id of child a parent process returns
  1270                              <1> 	;	= process id of parent when a child process returns
  1271                              <1> 	;
  1272                              <1> 	;       In original UNIX v1, sysfork is called and returns as
  1273                              <1> 	;	in following manner: (with an example: c library, fork)
  1274                              <1> 	;
  1275                              <1> 	;	1:
  1276                              <1> 	;		sys	fork
  1277                              <1> 	;			br 1f  / child process returns here
  1278                              <1> 	;		bes	2f     / parent process returns here
  1279                              <1> 	;		/ pid of new process in r0
  1280                              <1> 	;		rts	pc
  1281                              <1> 	;	2: / parent process condionally branches here
  1282                              <1> 	;		mov	$-1,r0 / pid = -1 means error return
  1283                              <1> 	;		rts	pc
  1284                              <1> 	;
  1285                              <1> 	;	1: / child process brances here
  1286                              <1> 	;		clr	r0   / pid = 0 in child process
  1287                              <1> 	;		rts	pc
  1288                              <1> 	;
  1289                              <1> 	;	In UNIX v7x86 (386) by Robert Nordier (1999)
  1290                              <1> 	;		// pid = fork();
  1291                              <1> 	;		//
  1292                              <1> 	;		// pid == 0 in child process;
  1293                              <1> 	;		// pid == -1 means error return
  1294                              <1> 	;		// in child,
  1295                              <1> 	;		//	parents id is in par_uid if needed
  1296                              <1> 	;
  1297                              <1> 	;		_fork:
  1298                              <1> 	;			mov	$.fork,eax
  1299                              <1> 	;			int	$0x30
  1300                              <1> 	;			jmp	1f
  1301                              <1> 	;			jnc	2f
  1302                              <1> 	;			jmp	cerror
  1303                              <1> 	;		1:
  1304                              <1> 	;			mov	eax,_par_uid
  1305                              <1> 	;			xor	eax,eax
  1306                              <1> 	;		2:
  1307                              <1> 	;			ret
  1308                              <1> 	;
  1309                              <1> 	;	In Retro UNIX 8086 v1,
  1310                              <1> 	;	'sysfork' returns in following manner:
  1311                              <1> 	;
  1312                              <1> 	;		mov	ax, sys_fork
  1313                              <1> 	;		mov	bx, offset @f ; routine for child
  1314                              <1> 	;		int	20h
  1315                              <1> 	;		jc	error
  1316                              <1> 	;
  1317                              <1> 	;	; Routine for parent process here (just after 'jc')
  1318                              <1> 	;		mov	word ptr [pid_of_child], ax
  1319                              <1> 	;		jmp	next_routine_for_parent
  1320                              <1> 	;

  1568                              <1> 	;            ("loc_INT21h_create_file")
  1569                              <1>         ; 	10/07/2011 (12/03/2011)
  1570                              <1>         ;	INT 21h Function AH = 3Ch
  1571                              <1>         ;	Create File
  1572                              <1>         ;	INPUT
  1573                              <1>         ;	   CX = Attributes
  1574                              <1>         ;          DS:DX= Address of zero terminaned path name
  1575                              <1>         ;
  1576                              <1> 	; 27/12/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1.1)
  1577                              <1> 	; 14/05/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
  1578                              <1> 	; 27/05/2013 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
  1579                              <1> 	;
  1580                              <1> 	; 'syscreat' called with two arguments; name and mode.
  1581                              <1> 	; u.namep points to name of the file and mode is put
  1582                              <1> 	; on the stack. 'namei' is called to get i-number of the file.
  1583                              <1> 	; If the file aready exists, it's mode and owner remain 
  1584                              <1> 	; unchanged, but it is truncated to zero length. If the file
  1585                              <1> 	; did not exist, an i-node is created with the new mode via
  1586                              <1> 	; 'maknod' whether or not the file already existed, it is
  1587                              <1> 	; open for writing. The fsp table is then searched for a free
  1588                              <1> 	; entry. When a free entry is found, proper data is placed
  1589                              <1> 	; in it and the number of this entry is put in the u.fp list.
  1590                              <1> 	; The index to the u.fp (also know as the file descriptor)
  1591                              <1> 	; is put in the user's r0.
  1592                              <1> 	;
  1593                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
  1594                              <1> 	;	syscreate; name; mode
  1595                              <1> 	; Arguments:
  1596                              <1> 	;	name - name of the file to be created
  1597                              <1> 	;	mode - mode of the file to be created
  1598                              <1> 	; Inputs: (arguments)
  1599                              <1> 	; Outputs: *u.r0 - index to u.fp list 
  1600                              <1> 	;		   (the file descriptor of new file)
  1601                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
  1602                              <1> 	;
  1603                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification:
  1604                              <1> 	;       'syscreate' system call has two arguments; so,
  1605                              <1> 	;	* 1st argument, name is pointed to by BX register
  1606                              <1> 	;	* 2nd argument, mode is in CX register
  1607                              <1> 	;
  1608                              <1> 	;	AX register (will be restored via 'u.r0') will return
  1609                              <1> 	;	to the user with the file descriptor/number
  1610                              <1> 	;	(index to u.fp list).
  1611                              <1> 	;
  1612                              <1> 	;call	arg2
  1613                              <1> 	; * name - 'u.namep' points to address of file/path name
  1614                              <1> 	;          in the user's program segment ('u.segmnt')
  1615                              <1> 	;          with offset in BX register (as sysopen argument 1).
  1616                              <1> 	; * mode - sysopen argument 2 is in CX register 
  1617                              <1> 	;          which is on top of stack.
  1618                              <1> 	;
  1619                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (10/10/2016)
  1620                              <1> 	;
  1621                              <1>         ; INPUT ->
  1622                              <1>         ;	   CL = File Attributes
  1623                              <1> 	;     	      bit 0 (1) - Read only file (R)
  1624                              <1> 	;             bit 1 (1) - Hidden file (H)
  1625                              <1>         ;             bit 2 (1) - System file (R)
  1626                              <1> 	;             bit 3 (1) - Volume label/name (V)
  1627                              <1>         ;             bit 4 (1) - Subdirectory (D)
  1628                              <1> 	;	      bit 5 (1) - File has been archived (A)
  1629                              <1>         ;          EBX = Pointer to filename (ASCIIZ) -path-
  1630                              <1> 	;
  1631                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
  1632                              <1> 	;          eax = File/Device Handle/Number (index) (AL)
  1633                              <1> 	;          cf = 1 -> Error code in AL
  1634                              <1> 	;
  1635                              <1> 	; Modified Registers: EAX (at the return of system call)
  1636                              <1> 	;
  1637                              <1> 	; Note: If the file is existing and it has not any one
  1638                              <1> 	;	of S,H,R,V,D attributes, it will be truncated
  1639                              <1> 	;	to zero length; otherwise, access error will be
  1640                              <1> 	;	returned.
  1641                              <1>
