  2036                              <1> 	;	     -derived from INT_21H.ASM-
  2037                              <1> 	;            ("loc_INT21h_open_file")
  2038                              <1>         ; 	26/02/2011 
  2039                              <1>         ;	INT 21h Function AH = 3Dh
  2040                              <1>         ;	Open File
  2041                              <1>         ;	INPUT
  2042                              <1>         ;	   AL= File Access Value
  2043                              <1> 	;     	     0- Open for reading
  2044                              <1> 	;            1- Open for writing
  2045                              <1>         ;            2- Open for reading and writing
  2046                              <1>         ;          DS:DX= Pointer to filename (ASCIIZ)
  2047                              <1>         ;
  2048                              <1> 	; 14/05/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
  2049                              <1> 	; 22/05/2013 - 27/05/2013 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
  2050                              <1> 	;
  2051                              <1> 	; 'sysopen' opens a file in following manner:
  2052                              <1> 	;    1) The second argument in a sysopen says whether to
  2053                              <1> 	;	open the file ro read (0) or write (>0).
  2054                              <1> 	;    2) I-node of the particular file is obtained via 'namei'.
  2055                              <1> 	;    3) The file is opened by 'iopen'.
  2056                              <1> 	;    4) Next housekeeping is performed on the fsp table
  2057                              <1> 	;	and the user's open file list - u.fp.
  2058                              <1> 	;	a) u.fp and fsp are scanned for the next available slot.
  2059                              <1> 	;	b) An entry for the file is created in the fsp table.
  2060                              <1> 	;	c) The number of this entry is put on u.fp list.
  2061                              <1> 	;	d) The file descriptor index to u.fp list is pointed
  2062                              <1> 	;	   to by u.r0.
  2063                              <1> 	;
  2064                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
  2065                              <1> 	;	sysopen; name; mode
  2066                              <1> 	; Arguments:
  2067                              <1> 	;	name - file name or path name
  2068                              <1> 	;	mode - 0 to open for reading
  2069                              <1> 	;	       1 to open for writing
  2070                              <1> 	; Inputs: (arguments)
  2071                              <1> 	; Outputs: *u.r0 - index to u.fp list (the file descriptor)
  2072                              <1> 	;		  is put into r0's location on the stack.
  2073                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
  2074                              <1> 	;
  2075                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification:
  2076                              <1> 	;       'sysopen' system call has two arguments; so,
  2077                              <1> 	;	* 1st argument, name is pointed to by BX register
  2078                              <1> 	;	* 2nd argument, mode is in CX register
  2079                              <1> 	;
  2080                              <1> 	;	AX register (will be restored via 'u.r0') will return
  2081                              <1> 	;	to the user with the file descriptor/number
  2082                              <1> 	;	(index to u.fp list).
  2083                              <1> 	;
  2084                              <1> 	;call	arg2
  2085                              <1> 	; * name - 'u.namep' points to address of file/path name
  2086                              <1> 	;          in the user's program segment ('u.segmnt')
  2087                              <1> 	;          with offset in BX register (as sysopen argument 1).
  2088                              <1> 	; * mode - sysopen argument 2 is in CX register
  2089                              <1> 	;          which is on top of stack.
  2090                              <1> 	;
  2091                              <1> 	; jsr r0,arg2 / get sys args into u.namep and on stack
  2092                              <1> 	;
  2093                              <1>        	; system call registers: ebx, ecx (through 'sysenter')
  2094                              <1> 	;
  2095                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (05/10/2016)
  2096                              <1> 	;
  2097                              <1>         ; INPUT ->
  2098                              <1>         ;	   CL = File Access Value (Open Mode)
  2099                              <1> 	;     	      0 - Open file for reading
  2100                              <1> 	;             1 - Open file for writing
  2101                              <1>         ;             2 - Open device for reading
  2102                              <1> 	;	      3 - Open device for writing
  2103                              <1>         ;          EBX = Pointer to filename/devicename (ASCIIZ)
  2104                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
  2105                              <1> 	;          eax = File/Device Handle/Number (index) (AL)
  2106                              <1> 	;          cf = 1 -> Error code in AL
  2107                              <1> 	;
  2108                              <1> 	; Modified Registers: EAX (at the return of system call)
  2109                              <1> 	;
  2110                              <1> 
  2111 0000E741 80F901              <1> 	cmp	cl, 1 ; read file (0), write file (1)
  2112 0000E744 7614                <1> 	jna	short sysopen_0

  2574                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5
  2575                              <1> 	; 15/10/2016
  2576                              <1> 	; 10/10/2016 (TRDOS 386 = TRDOS v2.0)
  2577                              <1> 	;	     -derived from INT_21H.ASM-
  2578                              <1> 	;            ("loc_INT21h_create_file")
  2579                              <1>         ; 	10/07/2011 (12/03/2011)
  2580                              <1>         ;	INT 21h Function AH = 3Ch
  2581                              <1>         ;	Create File
  2582                              <1>         ;	INPUT
  2583                              <1>         ;	   CX = Attributes
  2584                              <1>         ;          DS:DX= Address of zero terminaned path name
  2585                              <1>         ;
  2586                              <1>         ;
  2587                              <1> 	; 14/05/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
  2588                              <1> 	; 27/05/2013 - 02/08/2013 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
  2589                              <1> 	;
  2590                              <1> 	; 'sysmkdir' creates an empty directory whose name is
  2591                              <1> 	; pointed to by arg 1. The mode of the directory is arg 2.
  2592                              <1> 	; The special entries '.' and '..' are not present.
  2593                              <1> 	; Errors are indicated if the directory already exists or
  2594                              <1> 	; user is not the super user. 
  2595                              <1> 	;
  2596                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
  2597                              <1> 	;	sysmkdir; name; mode
  2598                              <1> 	; Arguments:
  2599                              <1> 	;	name - points to the name of the directory
  2600                              <1> 	;	mode - mode of the directory
  2601                              <1> 	; Inputs: (arguments)
  2602                              <1> 	; Outputs: -
  2603                              <1> 	;    (sets 'directory' flag to 1;
  2604                              <1> 	;    'set user id on execution' and 'executable' flags to 0)
  2605                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
  2606                              <1> 	;
  2607                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification: 
  2608                              <1> 	;       'sysmkdir' system call has two arguments; so,
  2609                              <1> 	;	* 1st argument, name is pointed to by BX register
  2610                              <1> 	;	* 2nd argument, mode is in CX register
  2611                              <1> 	;
  2612                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (10/10/2016)
  2613                              <1> 	;
  2614                              <1>         ; INPUT ->
  2615                              <1>         ;	   CL = Directory Attributes
  2616                              <1> 	;     	      bit 0 (1) - Read only file/dir (R)
  2617                              <1> 	;             bit 1 (1) - Hidden file/dir (H)
  2618                              <1>         ;             bit 2 (1) - System file/dir (R)
  2619                              <1> 	;             bit 3 (1) - Volume label/name (V)
  2620                              <1>         ;             bit 4 (1) - Subdirectory (D)
  2621                              <1> 	;	      bit 5 (1) - File/Dir has been archived (A)
  2622                              <1> 	;	   CX = 0 -> create normal directory
  2623                              <1>         ;          EBX = Pointer to directory name (ASCIIZ) -path-
  2624                              <1> 	;
  2625                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
  2626                              <1> 	;          eax = First cluster of the new directory
  2627                              <1> 	;          cf = 1 -> Error code in AL
  2628                              <1> 	;
  2629                              <1> 	; Modified Registers: EAX (at the return of system call)
  2630                              <1> 	;
  2631                              <1> 	; Note: If the file or directory is existing
  2632                              <1> 	;	an access error will be returned.
  2633                              <1> 
  2634 0000E8F0 6621C9              <1> 	and	cx, cx ; if cx = 0 -> create a normal subdir
  2635 0000E8F3 7414                <1> 	jz	short sysmkdir_1
  2636                              <1> 
  2637 0000E8F5 F6C110              <1> 	test	cl, 10h ; if dir flags set, also use other flags
  2638                              <1> 	;jnz	sysmkdir_0 ; jump to head of 'syscreat'
  2639                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022
  2640 0000E8F8 7405                <1> 	jz	short sysmkdir_invf
  2641                              <1> sysmkdir_3:
  2642 0000E8FA E914FDFFFF          <1> 	jmp	sysmkdir_0
  2643                              <1>

  2681                              <1> sysclose: ;<close file>
  2682                              <1> 	; 24/04/2025 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10
  2683                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
  2684                              <1> 	; 06/10/2016 (TRDOS 386 = TRDOS v2.0)
  2685                              <1> 	;
  2686                              <1> 	; 14/05/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
  2687                              <1> 	; 22/05/2013 - 26/05/2013 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
  2688                              <1> 	;
  2689                              <1> 	; 'sysclose', given a file descriptor in 'u.r0', closes the
  2690                              <1> 	; associated file. The file descriptor (index to 'u.fp' list)
  2691                              <1> 	; is put in r1 and 'fclose' is called.
  2692                              <1> 	;
  2693                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
  2694                              <1> 	;	sysclose
  2695                              <1> 	; Arguments:
  2696                              <1> 	;	-
  2697                              <1> 	; Inputs: *u.r0 - file descriptor
  2698                              <1> 	; Outputs: -
  2699                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
  2700                              <1> 	;
  2701                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification:
  2702                              <1> 	;	 The user/application program puts file descriptor
  2703                              <1> 	;        in BX register as 'sysclose' system call argument.
  2704                              <1> 	; 	 (argument transfer method 1)
  2705                              <1> 
  2706                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (06/10/2016)
  2707                              <1> 	;
  2708                              <1>         ; INPUT ->
  2709                              <1>         ;	   EBX = File Handle/Number (file index) (AL)
  2710                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
  2711                              <1> 	;          cf = 0 -> EAX = 0
  2712                              <1> 	;          cf = 1 -> Error code in EAX (ERR_FILE_NOT_OPEN)
  2713                              <1> 	;
  2714                              <1> 	; Modified Registers: EAX (at the return of system call)
  2715                              <1> 	;
  2716                              <1> 
  2717 0000E92D 89D8                <1> 	mov 	eax, ebx
  2718 0000E92F 31DB                <1> 	xor	ebx, ebx
  2719 0000E931 891D[A4B00100]      <1> 	mov	[u.r0], ebx ; 0  ; return value of EAX
  2720 0000E937 E83D310000          <1> 	call 	fclose
  2721                              <1> 	;jnc	sysret
  2722                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022
  2723 0000E93C 7205                <1> 	jc	short sysclose_err
  2724 0000E93E E956F8FFFF          <1> 	jmp	sysret
  2725                              <1> 
  2726                              <1> sysclose_err:
  2727                              <1> 	; 24/04/2025
  2728                              <1> 	;mov	eax, ERR_FILE_NOT_OPEN ; file not open !
  2729                              <1> 	;mov	[u.error], eax ;
  2730 0000E943 A1[F4B00100]        <1> 	mov	eax, [u.error]

  2737                              <1> 	; 14/01/2026

  2739                              <1> 	; 01/01/2026
  2740                              <1> 	; 08/12/2025 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10 (v2.1)
  2741                              <1> 	; 27/09/2024
  2742                              <1> 	; 18/09/2024
  2743                              <1> 	; 03/09/2024 (TRDOS v2.0.9)
  2744                              <1> 	; 11/10/2016 (TRDOS 386 = TRDOS v2.0)
  2745                              <1> 	;	     -derived from INT_21H.ASM-
  2746                              <1> 	;            ("loc_INT21h_read_file")
  2747                              <1>         ; 	13/03/2011 (05/03/2011)
  2748                              <1>         ;	INT 21h Function AH = 3Fh
  2749                              <1>         ;	Read from a File
  2750                              <1>         ;	INPUT
  2751                              <1> 	;	   BX = File Handle
  2752                              <1>         ;	   CX = Number of bytes to read
  2753                              <1>         ;          DS:DX= Buffer address
  2754                              <1>         ;
  2755                              <1> 	; Note: TRDOS 386 'sysread' has been derived from
  2756                              <1> 	;	Retro UNIX 386 v1 'sysread', except a few
  2757                              <1> 	;	code modifications.
  2758                              <1> 	;
  2759                              <1> 	; 13/05/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1)
  2760                              <1> 	; 11/05/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
  2761                              <1> 	; 23/05/2013 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
  2762                              <1> 	;
  2763                              <1> 	; 'sysread' is given a buffer to read into and the number of
  2764                              <1> 	; characters to be read. If finds the file from the file
  2765                              <1> 	; descriptor located in *u.r0 (r0). This file descriptor
  2766                              <1> 	; is returned from a successful open call (sysopen).
  2767                              <1> 	; The i-number of file is obtained via 'rw1' and the data
  2768                              <1> 	; is read into core via 'readi'.
  2769                              <1> 	;
  2770                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
  2771                              <1> 	;	sysread; buffer; nchars
  2772                              <1> 	; Arguments:
  2773                              <1> 	;	buffer - location of contiguous bytes where
  2774                              <1> 	;		 input will be placed.
  2775                              <1> 	;	nchars - number of bytes or characters to be read.
  2776                              <1> 	; Inputs: *u.r0 - file descriptor (& arguments)
  2777                              <1> 	; Outputs: *u.r0 - number of bytes read.
  2778                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
  2779                              <1> 	;
  2780                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification:
  2781                              <1> 	;       'sysread' system call has three arguments; so,
  2782                              <1> 	;	* 1st argument, file descriptor is in BX register
  2783                              <1> 	;	* 2nd argument, buffer address/offset in CX register
  2784                              <1> 	;	* 3rd argument, number of bytes is in DX register
  2785                              <1> 	;
  2786                              <1> 	;	AX register (will be restored via 'u.r0') will return
  2787                              <1> 	;	to the user with number of bytes read.
  2788                              <1> 	;
  2789                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (05/10/2016)
  2790                              <1> 	;
  2791                              <1>         ; INPUT ->
  2792                              <1>         ;	   EBX = File handle (descriptor/index)
  2793                              <1> 	;	   ECX = Buffer address
  2794                              <1>         ;          EDX = Number of bytes
  2795                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
  2796                              <1> 	;          EAX = Number of bytes have been read
  2797                              <1> 	;          cf = 1 -> Error code in AL

  2799                              <1> 	; Modified Registers: EAX (at the return of system call)

  2877                              <1> 	;

  2880                              <1> 	; Arguments:

  2889                              <1> 	;	* 1st argument, file descriptor is in BX register

  3137                              <1> 	; 18/05/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
  3138                              <1> 	; (TRDOS 386 feature only!)
  3139                              <1> 	;
  3140                              <1> 	; (start or stop timer event(s))
  3141                              <1> 	;
  3142                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
  3143                              <1> 	;	BL = Signal return byte (response byte)
  3144                              <1> 	;	     (Any requested value between 0 and 255)
  3145                              <1> 	;	     (Kernel will put it at the requested address)
  3146                              <1> 	;	BH = Time count unit
  3147                              <1> 	;	     0 = Stop timer event
  3148                              <1> 	;	     1 = 18.2 ticks per second
  3149                              <1> 	;	     2 = 10 milliseconds
  3150                              <1> 	;	     3 = 1 second (for real time clock interrupt)
  3151                              <1> 	;	     4 = time/tick count in current time count unit
  3152                              <1> 	;	    // 10/12/2016
  3153                              <1> 	;	    80h = Stop timer event (callback method)
  3154                              <1> 	;	    81h = 18.2 ticks per second, callback method
  3155                              <1> 	;	    82h = 10 milliseconds, callback method
  3156                              <1> 	;	    83h = 1 second (for RTC int), callback method
  3157                              <1> 	;	    84h = current time count unit, callback method
  3158                              <1> 	;
  3159                              <1> 	;	    Note: Only 03h or 83h will set real time clock
  3160                              <1> 	;		  (RTC) events (Others are for PIT events)!
  3161                              <1> 	;
  3162                              <1> 	;	NOTE: If callback (user service) method is used,
  3163                              <1> 	;	    EDX will point to the return address (of service
  3164                              <1> 	;	    procedure) in user's space instead of signal
  3165                              <1> 	;	    response byte address. (TRDOS 386 kernel will
  3166                              <1> 	;	    direct the cpu to that address -in user's space-
  3167                              <1> 	;	    at the return of system call or interrupt 
  3168                              <1> 	;	    just after the adjusted count/time is elapsed.)
  3169                              <1> 	;	    User's sevice routine must be ended with a
  3170                              <1> 	;	    'iret'. Normal return addresses from system
  3171                              <1> 	;	    calls or and interrupts will be kept same except
  3172                              <1> 	;	    the timer returns.
  3173                              <1>      	;
  3174                              <1> 	;	BH = 0 -> Stop timer event
  3175                              <1> 	;	BL = Timer event number (1 to 255) if BH = 0
  3176                              <1> 	;	     If BL = 0, all timer events (which are belongs
  3177                              <1> 	;	      to running process) will be stopped
  3178                              <1> 	;	ECX = Time/Tick count (depending on time count unit)
  3179                              <1> 	;	EDX = Signal return (Response) byte address
  3180                              <1> 	;	      (virtual address in user's memory space)
  3181                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
  3182                              <1> 	;	AL = Timer event number	(1 to 255) (max. value = 16)
  3183                              <1> 	;	IF BH Input = 0 & CF = 0 & AL = 0 ->
  3184                              <1> 	;	     timer event(s) has/have been stopped/finished
  3185                              <1> 	;	CF = 1 & AL = 0 -> no timer setting space to set
  3186                              <1> 	;	CF = 1 & AL > 0 -> timer count unit is not usable
  3187                              <1> 	;
  3188                              <1> 	;	NOTE: To modify a time count for a user function,
  3189                              <1> 	;	      at first, current timer event must be stopped
  3190                              <1> 	;	      then a new timer event (which is related with
  3191                              <1> 	;	      same user function) must be started.
  3192                              <1> 	;
  3193                              <1> 	;	      Signal return (response) byte may be used for
  3194                              <1> 	;	      several purposes. Kernel will put this value
  3195                              <1> 	;	      to requested address during timer interrupt,
  3196                              <1> 	;	      program/user can check this value to understand
  3197                              <1> 	;	      which event has been occurred and what is changed.
  3198                              <1> 	;	      (Multi timer events can share same signal address)
  3199                              <1> 	;
  3200                              <1> 	;	NOTE: If the process is running while the time count
  3201                              <1> 	;	      is reached, kernel will put signal return (response)
  3202                              <1> 	;	      byte value at requested address during timer
  3203                              <1> 	;	      interrupt and the process will continue to run.
  3204                              <1> 	;	      Program/process must call (jump to) it's timer event
  3205                              <1> 	;	      function as required, for checking the timer event
  3206                              <1> 	;	      status via signal return (response) byte address.
  3207                              <1> 	;
  3208                              <1> 	;	      If the process is not running (waiting or sleeping
  3209                              <1> 	;	      or released) while the time count is reached,
  3210                              <1> 	;	      it is restarted from where it left, to ensure
  3211                              <1> 	;	      proper multi media (video, audio, clock, timer)
  3212                              <1> 	;	      functionality.
  3213                              <1> 	;
  3214                              <1> 	;	      (It is better to use 'syswait' or 'syssleep',
  3215                              <1> 	;	      or 'sysrele' system call just after the timer
  3216                              <1> 	;	      function. Otherwise, timer events may block other
  3217                              <1> 	;	      processes which are not using timer events.)
  3218                              <1> 	;
  3219                              <1> 	; Timer Event Structure: (max. 16 timer events, 16*16 bytes)
  3220                              <1> 	;       Owner:	        resb 1 ; 0 = free
  3221                              <1> 	;		  	       ;>0 = process number (u.uno)
  3222                              <1> 	;	Calback:	resb 1 ; 1 = callback, 0 = response byte
  3223                              <1> 	;	Interrupt:      resb 1 ; 0 = Timer interrupt (or none)
  3224                              <1> 	;		   	       ; 1 = Real Time Clock interrupt
  3225                              <1> 	;	Response:       resb 1 ; 0 to 255, signal return value
  3226                              <1> 	;	Count Limit:	resd 1 ; count of ticks (total/set)
  3227                              <1> 	;	Current Count: 	resd 1 ; count of ticks (current)
  3228                              <1> 	;	Response Addr:  resd 1 ; response byte (pointer) address
  3229                              <1> 	;
  3230                              <1> 
  3231                              <1> 	; 19/12/2016 (timer callback)

  3507                              <1> 	; 16/05/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
  3508                              <1> 	;
  3509                              <1> 	; VIDEO DATA TRANSFER FUNCTIONS:
  3510                              <1> 	;
  3511                              <1> 	; Inputs:
  3512                              <1> 	;		; 07/02/2021
  3513                              <1> 	;	BH = 0 = VIDEO BIOS Mode 3, tty/text mode data transfers
  3514                              <1> 	;	     BL =
  3515                              <1> 	;		Bits 0&1, Transfer direction
  3516                              <1> 	;	     	 	0 - System to system
  3517                              <1> 	;			1 - User to system
  3518                              <1> 	;			2 - System to user
  3519                              <1> 	;			3 - Exhange (Swap) - 28/01/2021
  3520                              <1> 	;		Bits 2, Transfer Type
  3521                              <1> 	;			0 - Display page (complete) transfer
  3522                              <1> 	;	     		1 - Display page window (col,row) transfer
  3523                              <1> 	;		; 28/01/2021
  3524                              <1> 	;		Bits 3..7 - Reserved, undefined (must be 0)
  3525                              <1> 	;	        ; 28/01/2021
  3526                              <1> 	;	     /// BL = 0 -> System to system (display page) transfer
  3527                              <1> 	;		 CL = Source page (0FFh = current video page)
  3528                              <1> 	;		 DL = Destination page (0FFh = current video page)
  3529                              <1> 	;		 (Note: Nothing to do if src & dest are same page)
  3530                              <1> 	;	     /// BL = 1&2 -> user to system & system to user transfer
  3531                              <1> 	;		 ECX = User's buffer address
  3532                              <1> 	;		 DL = Video page (0FFh = current video page)
  3533                              <1> 	;	     /// BL = 3 -> exchange (swap) display page ; 28/01/2021
  3534                              <1> 	;		 ECX = User's buffer address
  3535                              <1> 	;		 DL = Video page (0FFh = current video page)
  3536                              <1> 	;		 EDI = Swap address in user's memory (must be > 0)
  3537                              <1> 	;	     /// BL = 5&6&7 -> user to system, system to user transfer
  3538                              <1> 	;		(system window is in current/active display page)
  3539                              <1> 	;		 ESI = User's buffer address
  3540                              <1> 	;		 ECX Low 16 bits = Top left column (X1 position)
  3541                              <1> 	;		 ECX High 16 bits = Top row (Y1 position)
  3542                              <1> 	;		 EDX Low 16 bits = Bottom right column (X2 position)
  3543                              <1> 	;		 EDX High 16 bits = Bottom row (Y2 position)
  3544                              <1>         ;                If BL = 5 or BL bit 0 & bit 1 are 1 ; 28/01/2021
  3545                              <1> 	;		 EDI = Swap address (in user's memory space)
  3546                              <1> 	;		 (If swap address > 0, previous content of the window
  3547                              <1> 	;		 will be saved into swap area in user's memory space)
  3548                              <1> 	;	     /// BL = 4 -> system to system transfer
  3549                              <1> 	;		 ESI = System's source buffer (video page) address
  3550                              <1> 	;		 ECX Low 16 bits = Top left column (X1 position)
  3551                              <1> 	;		 ECX High 16 bits = Top row (Y1 position)
  3552                              <1> 	;		 EDX Low 16 bits = Bottom right column (X2 position)
  3553                              <1> 	;		 EDX High 16 bits = Bottom row (Y2 position)
  3554                              <1> 	;		 EDI = System's destination buffer (video page) addr
  3555                              <1> 	;
  3556                              <1> 	;		; 06/02/2021
  3557                              <1> 	;		; 05/02/2021
  3558                              <1> 	;		; 01/02/2021, 02/02/2021
  3559                              <1> 	;		; 30/01/2021, 31/02/2021
  3560                              <1> 	;		; 29/01/2021 (major modification)
  3561                              <1> 	;		; 23/11/2020 (major modification)
  3562                              <1> 	;		; 22/11/2020 (bugfixes and extensions)
  3563                              <1> 	;	BH = 1 = VGA Graphics (0A0000h) data transfers
  3564                              <1> 	;		BL bit 7
  3565                              <1> 	;		   resolution (screen width) option
  3566                              <1> 	;		   0 = 320 pixels
  3567                              <1> 	;		   1 = 640 pixels
  3568                              <1> 	;		.. followings are same with SVGA transfer function
  3569                              <1> 	;		BL bit 6
  3570                              <1> 	;		   direction option
  3571                              <1> 	;		   0 = user to system (video memory)
  3572                              <1> 	;		   1 = system to user
  3573                              <1> 	;		BL bit 5
  3574                              <1> 	;		   masked/direct (non-masked) operations
  3575                              <1> 	;		   1 = masked, 0 = non-masked (direct)
  3576                              <1> 	;		BL bit 4
  3577                              <1> 	;		   page/window option
  3578                              <1> 	;		   1 = window, 0 = display page (screen)
  3579                              <1> 	;		BL bit 0 to 3 (pixel operation types)
  3580                              <1> 	;		   0 = Copy pixels (colors) ((mask color))
  3581                              <1> 	;		   1 = Change (New, Fill) color
  3582                              <1> 	;		   2 = Add color
  3583                              <1> 	;		   3 = Sub color
  3584                              <1> 	;		   4 = OR color
  3585                              <1> 	;		   5 = AND color
  3586                              <1> 	;		   6 = XOR color
  3587                              <1> 	;		   7 = NOT color
  3588                              <1> 	;		   8 = NEG color
  3589                              <1> 	;		   9 = INC color
  3590                              <1> 	;		  10 = DEC color
  3591                              <1> 	;		  11 = Mix (Average) colors
  3592                              <1> 	;		  12 = Replace pixel colors
  3593                              <1> 	;		  13 = Copy pixel block(s)
  3594                              <1> 	;		  14 = Write line(s)
  3595                              <1> 	;		  15 = Write character (font)
  3596                              <1> 	;
  3597                              <1> 	;	   Input Registers for pixel operations:
  3598                              <1> 	;		 Same with LFB data transfer function below
  3599                              <1> 	;
  3600                              <1> 	;		; 25/02/2021
  3601                              <1> 	;		; 05/02/2021, 06/02/2021
  3602                              <1> 	;		; 01/02/2021, 02/02/2021
  3603                              <1> 	;		; 30/01/2021, 31/02/2021
  3604                              <1> 	; 		; 29/01/2021 (major modification)
  3605                              <1> 	;		; 23/11/2020 (major modification)
  3606                              <1> 	;		; 22/11/2020 (bugfixes and extensions)
  3607                              <1> 	;	BH = 2 = Super VGA, LINEAR FRAME BUFFER data transfers
  3608                              <1> 	;		BL bit 7
  3609                              <1> 	;		   unused (invalid), must be 0
  3610                              <1> 	;		BL bit 6
  3611                              <1> 	;		   direction option
  3612                              <1> 	;		   0 = user to system (video memory)
  3613                              <1> 	;		   1 = system to user
  3614                              <1> 	;		BL bit 5
  3615                              <1> 	;		   masked/direct (non-masked) operations
  3616                              <1> 	;		   1 = masked, 0 = non-masked (direct)
  3617                              <1> 	;		BL bit 4
  3618                              <1> 	;		   page/window option
  3619                              <1> 	;		   1 = window, 0 = display page (screen)
  3620                              <1> 	;		BL bit 0 to 3 (pixel operation types)
  3621                              <1> 	;		   0 = Copy pixels (colors) ((mask color))
  3622                              <1> 	;		   1 = Change (New, Fill) color
  3623                              <1> 	;		   2 = Add color
  3624                              <1> 	;		   3 = Sub color
  3625                              <1> 	;		   4 = OR color
  3626                              <1> 	;		   5 = AND color
  3627                              <1> 	;		   6 = XOR color
  3628                              <1> 	;		   7 = NOT color
  3629                              <1> 	;		   8 = NEG color
  3630                              <1> 	;		   9 = INC color
  3631                              <1> 	;		  10 = DEC color
  3632                              <1> 	;		  11 = Mix (Average) colors
  3633                              <1> 	;		  12 = Replace pixel colors
  3634                              <1> 	;		  13 = Copy pixel block(s)
  3635                              <1> 	;		  14 = Write line(s)
  3636                              <1> 	;		  15 = Write character (font)
  3637                              <1> 	;
  3638                              <1> 	;	   Note: If HW of EBX > 0, it is VESA VBE mode number
  3639                              <1> 	;		 otherwise, function will be applied
  3640                              <1> 	;		 to current (VESA VBE) video mode.
  3641                              <1> 	;
  3642                              <1> 	;	   Input Registers for pixel operations:
  3643                              <1> 	;		-- user to system & system to system --
  3644                              <1> 	;		-- (BL = 0 to 0Fh) -- non-masked, screen --
  3645                              <1> 	;		-- (BL = 10h to 1Fh) -- non-masked, window --
  3646                              <1> 	;		-- (BL = 20h to 2Fh) -- masked, screen --
  3647                              <1> 	;		-- (BL = 30h to 3Fh) -- masked, window --
  3648                              <1> 	;		(*) window, (**) masked (***) sys to sys
  3649                              <1> 	;		for BL bit 0 to 3
  3650                              <1> 	;		00h: COPY PIXELS
  3651                              <1> 	;		  If BL bit 4 = 0 ; 21/02/2021
  3652                              <1> 	;		     full screen copy
  3653                              <1>    	;		     ECX & EDX will not be used
  3654                              <1> 	;		    (user buffer must fit to display page)
  3655                              <1> 	;		  If BL bit 4 = 1 ; 21/02/2021
  3656                              <1> 	;		    ECX = start position (row, column) (*)
  3657                              <1> 	;			  (HW = row, CX = column)
  3658                              <1> 	;		    EDX = size (rows, colums) (*)
  3659                              <1> 	;			  (HW = rows, DX = columns)
  3660                              <1> 	;		          (0 -> invalid)
  3661                              <1> 	;		          (1 -> horizontal or vertical line)
  3662                              <1> 	;		    ESI = user's buffer address
  3663                              <1> 	;		    EDI = mask color (**) ; 25/02/2021
  3664                              <1> 	;			  (this color will be excluded)
  3665                              <1> 	;		01h: CHANGE PIXEL COLORS
  3666                              <1> 	;		02h: ADD PIXEL COLORS
  3667                              <1> 	;		03h: SUB PIXEL COLORS
  3668                              <1> 	;		04h: OR PIXEL COLORS
  3669                              <1> 	;		05h: AND PIXEL COLORS
  3670                              <1> 	;		06h: XOR PIXEL COLORS
  3671                              <1> 	;		0Bh: MIX PIXEL COLORS
  3672                              <1> 	;		     CL = color (8 bit, 256 colors)
  3673                              <1> 	;		    ECX = color (16 bit and true colors)
  3674                              <1> 	;		    EDX = start position (row, column) (*)
  3675                              <1> 	;			 (HW = row, DX = column)
  3676                              <1> 	;		    ESI = size (rows, colums) (*)
  3677                              <1> 	;			  (HW = rows, SI = columns)
  3678                              <1> 	;		    EDI = mask color (**) ; 25/02/2021
  3679                              <1> 	;			  (this color will be excluded)
  3680                              <1> 	;		07h: NOT PIXEL COLORS
  3681                              <1> 	;		08h: NEG PIXEL COLORS
  3682                              <1> 	;		09h: INC PIXEL COLORS
  3683                              <1> 	;		0Ah: DEC PIXEL COLORS
  3684                              <1> 	;		    ECX = start position (row, column) (*)
  3685                              <1> 	;			  (HW = row, CX = column)
  3686                              <1> 	;		    EDX = size (rows, colums) (*)
  3687                              <1> 	;			  (HW = rows, DX = columns)
  3688                              <1> 	;		          (0 -> invalid)
  3689                              <1> 	;		          (1 -> horizontal or vertical line)
  3690                              <1> 	;		    EDI = mask color (**) ; 25/02/2021
  3691                              <1> 	;			  (this color will be excluded)
  3692                              <1> 	;		0Ch: REPLACE PIXEL COLORS
  3693                              <1> 	;		     CL = current color (8 bit, 256 colors)
  3694                              <1> 	;		    ECX = current color (16 bit and true colors)
  3695                              <1> 	;		     DL = new color (8 bit, 256 colors)
  3696                              <1> 	;		    EDX = new color (16 bit and true colors)
  3697                              <1> 	;		    ESI = start position (row, column) (*)
  3698                              <1> 	;			  (HW = row, SI = column)
  3699                              <1> 	;		    EDI = size (rows, colums) (*)
  3700                              <1> 	;			  (HW = rows, DI = columns)
  3701                              <1> 	;		0Dh: COPY PIXEL BLOCK(S) -full screen-
  3702                              <1> 	;		   -If BL bit 5 is 0-
  3703                              <1> 	;		    ECX = start position (row, column) (*)
  3704                              <1> 	;			  (HW = row, CX = column)
  3705                              <1> 	;		    EDX = size (rows, colums) (*)
  3706                              <1> 	;			  (HW = rows, DX = columns)
  3707                              <1> 	;		          (0 -> invalid)
  3708                              <1> 	;		          (1 -> horizontal or vertical line)
  3709                              <1> 	;		    ESI = destination (row, column) (***)
  3710                              <1> 	;		   -If BL bit 5 is 1-
  3711                              <1> 	;	               CL = color (8 bit, 256 colors)
  3712                              <1> 	;		      ECX = color (16 bit and true colors)
  3713                              <1> 	;	   	      EDX = count of blocks (not bytes)
  3714                              <1> 	;			    (limit: 2048 blocks)
  3715                              <1> 	;		      ESI = user's buffer address
  3716                              <1> 	;			  contains 64 bits block data
  3717                              <1> 	;			  BLOCK ADDRESS - (row, col), dword
  3718                              <1> 	;			  (first 32 bits)
  3719                              <1> 	;			  BLOCK SIZE - (rows, cols), dword
  3720                              <1> 	;			  (second 32 bits)
  3721                              <1> 	;		; 10/02/2021
  3722                              <1> 	;		0Eh: WRITE LINE(s) -full screen-
  3723                              <1> 	;		   -If BL bit 5 is 0-
  3724                              <1> 	; 		    CL = color (8 bit, 256 colors)
  3725                              <1> 	; 		   ECX = color (16 bit and true colors)
  3726                              <1> 	; 		    DX = low 12 bits - size (length)
  3727                              <1> 	;			 high 4 bits - direction or type
  3728                              <1> 	;			     0 - Horizontal line
  3729                              <1> 	;			     1 - Vertical line
  3730                              <1> 	;			   > 1 - undefined, invalid
  3731                              <1> 	; 		   ESI = start position (row, column)
  3732                              <1> 	;			 (HW = row, SI = column)
  3733                              <1> 	;		   -If BL bit 5 is 1-
  3734                              <1> 	;		     CL = color (8 bit, 256 colors)
  3735                              <1> 	;		    ECX = color (16 bit and true colors)
  3736                              <1> 	;		     DX = number of lines (in user buffer)
  3737                              <1> 	;			   (limit: 2048 lines)
  3738                              <1> 	;		    ESI = user's buffer
  3739                              <1> 	;		          contains 64 bit data for lines
  3740                              <1> 	;			   START POINT: 32 bit (row, col)
  3741                              <1> 	;			   LENGTH: 32 bit
  3742                              <1> 	;			   high 16 bits - 0
  3743                              <1> 	;			   bit 0-11 - length
  3744                              <1> 	;			   bit 12-15 - type (length)
  3745                              <1> 	;		0Fh: WRITE CHARACTER (FONT)
  3746                              <1> 	;		     CL = char's color (8 bit, 256 colors)
  3747                              <1> 	;		    ECX = char's color (16 bit and true colors)
  3748                              <1> 	;		     DL = Character's ASCII code
  3749                              <1> 	;		     DH bit 0 -> font height
  3750                              <1> 	;			  0 -> 8x16 character font
  3751                              <1> 	;			  1 -> 8x8 character font
  3752                              <1> 	;		     DH bit 1 & 2 -> scale
  3753                              <1> 	;			  0 = 1/1 (8 pixels per char row)
  3754                              <1> 	;			  1 = 2/1 (16 pixels per char row)
  3755                              <1> 	;			  2 = 3/1 (24 pixels per char row)
  3756                              <1> 	;			  3 = 4/1 (32 pixels per char row)
  3757                              <1> 	;		     DH bit 6 -> [ufont] option (1 = use [ufont])
  3758                              <1> 	;		     If DH bit 7 = 1
  3759                              <1> 	;			 USER FONT (from user buffer)
  3760                              <1> 	;			    DL = 0 -> 8x8 (width: 1 byte per row)
  3761                              <1> 	;			    DL = 1 -> 8x16
  3762                              <1> 	;			    DL = 2 -> 16x16 (width: 2 bytes)
  3763                              <1> 	;			    DL = 3 -> 16x32
  3764                              <1> 	;			    DL = 4 -> 24x24 (width: 3 bytes)
  3765                              <1> 	;			    DL = 5 -> 24x48
  3766                              <1> 	;			    DL = 6 -> 32x32 (width: 4 bytes)
  3767                              <1> 	;			    DL = 7 -> 32x64
  3768                              <1> 	;			    DL > 7 -> invalid (unused)
  3769                              <1> 	;			 EDI = user's font buffer address
  3770                              <1> 	;			    (NOTE: byte order is as row0,row1,row2..)
  3771                              <1> 	; 		    ESI = start position (row, column) (*)
  3772                              <1> 	;			     (HW = row, SI = column)
  3773                              <1> 	;
  3774                              <1> 	;		-- system to user --
  3775                              <1> 	;		   BL (bit 0 to 7)
  3776                              <1> 	;	 	40h: COPY PIXELS (full screen, display page)
  3777                              <1> 	;		    EDI = user's buffer address
  3778                              <1> 	;		41h: COPY PIXELS (window)
  3779                              <1> 	;		    ECX = start position (row, column) (*)
  3780                              <1> 	;			  (HW = row, CX = column)
  3781                              <1> 	;		    EDX = size (rows, colums) (*)
  3782                              <1> 	;			  (HW = rows, DX = columns)
  3783                              <1> 	;		          (<=1 -> horizontal or vertical line)
  3784                              <1> 	;		    EDI = user's buffer address
  3785                              <1> 	;
  3786                              <1> 	;		Example: (29/01/2021)
  3787                              <1> 	;		    ecx = 00400064h (start at row 64, column 100)
  3788                              <1> 	;		    edx = 00320048h (size: 50 rows, 72 columns)
  3789                              <1> 	;				    (end at row 114, column 172)
  3790                              <1> 	;		    If video memory starts at 0A0000h
  3791                              <1> 	;		    and if resolution is 320x200 (256 colors) ..
  3792                              <1> 	;		    window start offset: (64*320)+100 = 20580
  3793                              <1> 	;		    window size: 16072 bytes (pixels) 
  3794                              <1> 	;		    window end offset: 20580+16072 = 36652
  3795                              <1> 	;		    window start address: 0A0000h+564h = 0A5064h
  3796                              <1> 	; Outputs:
  3797                              <1> 	;	EAX = transfer/byte count
  3798                              <1> 	;
  3799                              <1> 	;	NOTE: If the source or destination address passes out of
  3800                              <1> 	;	video pages (display memory limits), data will not be transferred
  3801                              <1> 	;	and EAX will return as 0.
  3802                              <1> 	;
  3803                              <1> 	; 08/02/2021
  3804                              <1> 	; 07/02/2021
  3805                              <1> 	; 04/01/2021
  3806                              <1> 	; PIXEL READ/WRITE (in current/active video mode)
  3807                              <1> 	;
  3808                              <1> 	;	BH = 3 = Read/Write pixel(s) -for all graphics modes-
  3809                              <1> 	;	     BL = 
  3810                              <1> 	;		0 = Read pixel
  3811                              <1> 	;		1 = Write pixel
  3812                              <1> 	;	     	2 = swap pixel colors
  3813                              <1> 	;		3 = mix pixel colors
  3814                              <1> 	;	     29/01/2021
  3815                              <1> 	;		4 = read pixels from user defined positions
  3816                              <1> 	;		5 = write single color pixels to user defined positions
  3817                              <1> 	;		6 = write multi color pixels to user defined positions
  3818                              <1> 	;
  3819                              <1> 	;	      > 6 = invalid/unimplemented
  3820                              <1> 	;
  3821                              <1> 	;	     .. for BL = 0 to 5
  3822                              <1> 	;	     CL = color for writing pixel(s) or
  3823                              <1>  	;	     ECX = color for writing pixel(s) in true color modes
  3824                              <1> 	;
  3825                              <1> 	;	     EDX = Offset from start of video memory (0A0000h)
  3826                              <1> 	;		   or start of linear frame buffer
  3827                              <1> 	;
  3828                              <1> 	;	     07/02/2021	
  3829                              <1> 	;	     .. for BL = 4
  3830                              <1> 	;	     EDI = user's destination buffer address for pixel colors
  3831                              <1> 	;	     29/01/2021

  3976                              <1> 	;		  bit 2%3 -> green level (0,1,2,3)
  3977                              <1> 	;		  bit 0&1 -> red level (0,1,2,3)

  3979                              <1> 	;	      Luminosity base level: 0 -> 16
  3980                              <1> 	;		 		     1 -> 32

  3990                              <1> 	;	     Color levels: Color values are fixed to (nearest)
  3991                              <1> 	;		   one of all possible set level (step) values
  3992                              <1> 	;		   (according to luminosity base level); then
  3993                              <1> 	;		   color levels are set to R-L, G-L, B-L.
  3994                              <1> 	;	 For example: If luminosity base level is 32
  3995                              <1> 	;		  all possible set values are 0, 32, 96, 255.
  3996                              <1> 	;
  3997                              <1> 	;	    * RGB (TRUE) colors to 16 colors conversion:

  3999                              <1> 	;	    	   If any one of R,G,B >= 128 L = 1
  4000                              <1>  	;		   If max. value of (R,G,B) >= 32, it is 1
  4001                              <1> 	;		      else all color bits (R&G&B&L) are 0

  4004                              <1> 	;		   If the third value >= max. value / 2

  4092                              <1> 	;	BH = 10 = Map video memory to user's buffer
  4093                              <1> 	;

  4099                              <1> 	;	EDX = Buffer size in bytes (if BL = 2)

  4115                              <1> 	; 04/01/2021
  4116                              <1> 	; SET/READ COLOR PALETTE (set/read DAC color registers)
  4117                              <1> 	;	((256 colors (8bpp) VGA/CGA video hardware feature))
  4118                              <1> 	;
  4119                              <1> 	;	BH = 11 = Set/Read DAC color registers
  4120                              <1> 	;
  4121                              <1> 	;	   (BL<4 Original method for std VGA video hardware)
  4122                              <1> 	;	   BL = 0 : Read all DAC color registers (256 colors)
  4123                              <1> 	;	       (6 bit colors, in RGB order)
  4124                              <1> 	;	   BL = 1 : Set all DAC color registers (256 colors)
  4125                              <1> 	;	       (6 bit colors, in RGB order)
  4126                              <1> 	;	   BL = 2 : Read single DAC color register
  4127                              <1> 	;	       (6 bit color, in RGB order)
  4128                              <1> 	;		((EAX will return with color value))
  4129                              <1> 	;		CL = DAC color register (index)
  4130                              <1> 	;	   BL = 3 : Set/Write single DAC color register
  4131                              <1> 	;	       (6 bit color, in RGB order, bit 6&7 are 0)
  4132                              <1> 	;		ECX byte 0 - DAC color register
  4133                              <1> 	;		ECX byte 1 - Red (6 bit)
  4134                              <1> 	;		ECX byte 2 - Green (6 bit)
  4135                              <1> 	;		ECX byte 3 - Blue (6 bit)
  4136                              <1> 	;	   (BL>3 Alternative method for BMP files etc.)
  4137                              <1> 	;	   BL = 4 : Read all DAC color registers (256 colors)
  4138                              <1> 	;	       (8 bit colors, in BGR order, bit 0&1 is 0)
  4139                              <1> 	;	   BL = 5 : Set all DAC color registers (256 colors)
  4140                              <1> 	;	       (8 bit colors, in BGR order, bit 0&1 is 0)
  4141                              <1> 	;	   BL = 6 : Read single DAC color register
  4142                              <1> 	;	       (8 bit color, in BGR order, bit 0&1 is 0)
  4143                              <1> 	;		((EAX will return with color value))
  4144                              <1> 	;		CL = DAC color register (index)
  4145                              <1> 	;	   BL = 7 : Set/Write single DAC color register
  4146                              <1> 	;	       (8 bit color, bit 0&1 are 0)
  4147                              <1> 	;		ECX byte 0 - DAC color register
  4148                              <1> 	;		ECX byte 1 - Blue (8 bit)
  4149                              <1> 	;		ECX byte 2 - Green (8 bit)
  4150                              <1> 	;		ECX byte 3 - Red (8 bit)
  4151                              <1> 	;
  4152                              <1> 	;	  BL > 7 : invalid (not implemented)
  4153                              <1> 	;
  4154                              <1> 	;   if BL bit 2 is 1, 6 bit colors converted to 8 bit colors
  4155                              <1> 	;	(low two bits of color bytes will be 0)
  4156                              <1> 	;     ((color byte 00111111b will be converted to 11111100b))
  4157                              <1> 	;	and RGB byte order will be
  4158                              <1> 	;		byte 0 - Blue (low 2 bits are 0)
  4159                              <1> 	;		byte 1 - Green (low 2 bits are 0)
  4160                              <1> 	;		byte 2 - Red (low 2 bits are 0)
  4161                              <1> 	;		byte 3 - pad (or zero byte)
  4162                              <1> 	;	and 256 colors buffer size must be 256*4 = 1024 bytes
  4163                              <1> 	;   if BL bit 2 is 0, 6 bit colors will be used directly
  4164                              <1> 	;	  (high two bits of 8 bit color bytes will be 0)
  4165                              <1> 	;     ((dac color 111111b will be converted to 00111111b))
  4166                              <1> 	;		byte 0 - Red (high 2 bits are 0)
  4167                              <1> 	;		byte 1 - Green (high 2 bits are 0)
  4168                              <1> 	;		byte 2 - Blue (high 2 bits are 0)
  4169                              <1> 	;	and 256 colors buffer size must be 256*3 = 768 bytes
  4170                              <1> 	;
  4171                              <1> 	;	ECX = User's buffer addr (256*3 = 768 bytes) or
  4172                              <1> 	;	      Color
  4173                              <1> 	;
  4174                              <1> 	; Return:

  6626                              <1> 	; INPUT:
  6627                              <1> 	;   -If BL bit 5 is 0-

  6743                              <1> pix_op_lin:
  6744                              <1> 	; 11/08/2022
  6745                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
  6746                              <1> 	; 12/02/2021

  6750                              <1> 	; 02/02/2021
  6751                              <1> 	; WRITE LINE -direct-
  6752                              <1> 	; WRITE LINE(S) -via user's buffer-
  6753                              <1> 	;
  6754                              <1> 	; INPUT:
  6755                              <1> 	;   -If BL bit 5 is 0-	
  6756                              <1> 	;     CL = color (8 bit, 256 colors)
  6757                              <1> 	;    ECX = color (16 bit and true colors)
  6758                              <1> 	;     DX = low 12 bits - size (length)
  6759                              <1> 	;	   high 4 bits - direction or type
  6760                              <1> 	;	     0 - Horizontal line
  6761                              <1> 	;	     1 - Vertical line
  6762                              <1> 	;	   > 1 - undefined, invalid
  6763                              <1> 	;    ESI = start position (row, column)
  6764                              <1> 	;	  (HW = row, SI = column)
  6765                              <1> 	;   -If BL bit 5 is 1-
  6766                              <1> 	;     CL = color (8 bit, 256 colors)
  6767                              <1> 	;    ECX = color (16 bit and true colors)
  6768                              <1> 	;     DX = number of lines (in user buffer)
  6769                              <1> 	;	   (limit: 2048 lines)	
  6770                              <1> 	;    ESI = user's buffer
  6771                              <1> 	;          contains 64 bit data for lines
  6772                              <1> 	;	   START POINT: 32 bit (row, col)
  6773                              <1> 	;	   LENGTH: 32 bit
  6774                              <1> 	;		   high 16 bits - 0
  6775                              <1> 	;		   bit 0-11 - length
  6776                              <1> 	;	   	   bit 12-15 - type (length)
  6777                              <1> 	; OUTPUT:
  6778                              <1> 	; 	[u.r0] will be > 0 if succesful
  6779                              <1> 
  6780                              <1> 	; Window option ([v_ops] bit 4) will be ignored

  7746                              <1> pix_op_chr:
  7747                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
  7748                              <1> 	; 15/02/2021
  7749                              <1> 	; 05/02/2021
  7750                              <1> 	; WRITE CHARACTER (FONT)
  7751                              <1> 	; 05/01/2021 ([ufont])
  7752                              <1> 	; 01/01/2021
  7753                              <1> 	;     CL = char's color (8 bit, 256 colors)
  7754                              <1> 	;    ECX = char's color (16 bit and true colors)
  7755                              <1> 	;     DL = Character's ASCII code
  7756                              <1> 	;     DH bit 0 -> font height
  7757                              <1> 	;	  0 -> 8x16 character font
  7758                              <1> 	;	  1 -> 8x8 character font
  7759                              <1> 	;     DH bit 1 & 2 -> scale
  7760                              <1> 	;	  0 = 1/1 (8 pixels per char row)
  7761                              <1> 	;	  1 = 2/1 (16 pixels per char row)
  7762                              <1> 	;	  2 = 3/1 (24 pixels per char row)

 12070                              <1> sysexec:
 12071                              <1> 	; 15/07/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.1.0 
 12072                              <1> 	; 13/07/2026
 12073                              <1> 	; 12/07/2026
 12074                              <1> 	; 11/07/2026
 12075                              <1> 	; 10/07/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.11
 12076                              <1> 	; 07/07/2025 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10 ; (v2.1.0)
 12077                              <1> 	; 21/08/2024 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.9
 12078                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
 12079                              <1> 	; 06/02/2022 - Retro UNIX 386 v1.2
 12080                              <1> 	; 18/11/2017
 12081                              <1> 	; 14/11/2017
 12082                              <1> 	; 13/11/2017
 12083                              <1> 	; 24/10/2016 - 04/01/2017
 12084                              <1> 	; 24/04/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
 12085                              <1> 	; 23/06/2015 - 23/10/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1)
 12086                              <1> 	; 03/06/2013 - 06/12/2013 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 12087                              <1> 	;
 12088                              <1> 	; 'sysexec' initiates execution of a file whose path name if
 12089                              <1> 	; pointed to by 'name' in the sysexec call.
 12090                              <1> 	; 'sysexec' performs the following operations:
 12091                              <1> 	;    1. obtains i-number of file to be executed via 'namei'.
 12092                              <1> 	;    2. obtains i-node of file to be exceuted via 'iget'.
 12093                              <1> 	;    3. sets trap vectors to system routines.
 12094                              <1> 	;    4. loads arguments to be passed to executing file into
 12095                              <1> 	;	highest locations of user's core
 12096                              <1> 	;    5. puts pointers to arguments in locations immediately
 12097                              <1> 	;	following arguments.
 12098                              <1> 	;    6.	saves number of arguments in next location.
 12099                              <1> 	;    7. initializes user's stack area so that all registers
 12100                              <1> 	;	will be zeroed and the PS is cleared and the PC set
 12101                              <1> 	;	to core when 'sysret' restores registers
 12102                              <1> 	;	and does an rti.
 12103                              <1> 	;    8. initializes u.r0 and u.sp
 12104                              <1> 	;    9. zeros user's core down to u.r0
 12105                              <1> 	;   10.	reads executable file from storage device into core
 12106                              <1> 	;	starting at location 'core'.
 12107                              <1> 	;   11.	sets u.break to point to end of user's code with
 12108                              <1> 	;	data area appended.
 12109                              <1> 	;   12.	calls 'sysret' which returns control at location
 12110                              <1> 	;	'core' via 'rti' instruction.
 12111                              <1> 	;
 12112                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
 12113                              <1> 	;	sysexec; namep; argp
 12114                              <1> 	; Arguments:
 12115                              <1> 	;	namep - points to pathname of file to be executed
 12116                              <1> 	;	argp  - address of table of argument pointers
 12117                              <1> 	;	argp1... argpn - table of argument pointers
 12118                              <1> 	;	argp1:<...0> ... argpn:<...0> - argument strings
 12119                              <1> 	; Inputs: (arguments)
 12120                              <1> 	; Outputs: -
 12121                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
 12122                              <1> 	;
 12123                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 386 v1 modification:
 12124                              <1> 	;	User application runs in it's own virtual space
 12125                              <1> 	;	which is izolated from kernel memory (and other
 12126                              <1> 	;	memory pages) via 80386	paging in ring 3
 12127                              <1> 	;	privilige mode. Virtual start address is always 0.
 12128                              <1> 	;	User's core memory starts at linear address 400000h
 12129                              <1> 	;	(the end of the 1st 4MB).
 12130                              <1> 	;
 12131                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification:
 12132                              <1> 	;	user/application segment and system/kernel segment
 12133                              <1> 	;	are different and sysenter/sysret/sysrele routines
 12134                              <1> 	;	are different (user's registers are saved to
 12135                              <1> 	;	and then restored from system's stack.)
 12136                              <1> 	;
 12137                              <1> 	;	NOTE: Retro UNIX 8086 v1 'arg2' routine gets these
 12138                              <1> 	;	      arguments which were in these registers;
 12139                              <1> 	;	      but, it returns by putting the 1st argument
 12140                              <1> 	;	      in 'u.namep' and the 2nd argument
 12141                              <1> 	;	      on top of stack. (1st argument is offset of the
 12142                              <1> 	;	      file/path name in the user's program segment.)
 12143                              <1> 
 12144                              <1> 	;call	arg2
 12145                              <1> 	; * name - 'u.namep' points to address of file/path name
 12146                              <1> 	;          in the user's program segment ('u.segmnt')
 12147                              <1> 	;          with offset in BX register (as sysopen argument 1).
 12148                              <1> 	; * argp - sysexec argument 2 is in CX register 
 12149                              <1> 	;          which is on top of stack.
 12150                              <1> 	;
 12151                              <1> 		; jsr r0,arg2 / arg0 in u.namep,arg1 on top of stack
 12152                              <1> 
 12153                              <1> 	; 23/06/2015 (32 bit modifications)
 12154                              <1> 
 12155                              <1> 	;; 13/11/2017
 12156                              <1> 	;;mov	[u.namep], ebx ; argument 1
 12157                              <1>         ; 18/10/2015

 12852                              <1> fclose:
 12853                              <1> 	; 05/09/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.1.0
 12854                              <1> 	; 16/01/2026
 12855                              <1> 	; 02/01/2026
 12856                              <1> 	; 24/04/2025
 12857                              <1> 	; 21/04/2025 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.10 (v2.1 pre-work)
 12858                              <1> 	; 18/09/2024 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.9
 12859                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5
 12860                              <1> 	; 06/10/2016 (TRDOS 386 = TRDOS v2.0)
 12861                              <1> 	;
 12862                              <1> 	; 18/06/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
 12863                              <1> 	;            (32 bit offset pointer modification)
 12864                              <1> 	; 19/04/2013 - 12/01/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 12865                              <1> 	;
 12866                              <1> 	; Given the file descriptor (index to the u.fp list)
 12867                              <1> 	; 'fclose' first gets the i-number of the file via 'getf'.
 12868                              <1> 	; If i-node is active (i-number > 0) the entry in
 12869                              <1> 	; u.fp list is cleared. If all the processes that opened
 12870                              <1> 	; that file close it, then fsp entry is freed and the file
 12871                              <1> 	; is closed. If not a return is taken.
 12872                              <1> 	; If the file has been deleted while open, 'anyi' is called
 12873                              <1> 	; to see anyone else has it open, i.e., see if it is appears
 12874                              <1> 	; in another entry in the fsp table. Upon return from 'anyi'
 12875                              <1> 	; a check is made to see if the file is special.
 12876                              <1> 	;
 12877                              <1> 	; INPUTS ->
 12878                              <1> 	;    r1 - contains the file descriptor (value=0,1,2...)
 12879                              <1> 	;    u.fp - list of entries in the fsp table
 12880                              <1> 	;    fsp - table of entries (4 words/entry) of open files.
 12881                              <1> 	; OUTPUTS ->
 12882                              <1> 	;    r1 - contains the same file descriptor
 12883                              <1> 	;    r2 - contains i-number
 12884                              <1> 	;
 12885                              <1> 	; ((AX = R1))
 12886                              <1> 	; ((Modified registers: EDX, EBX, ECX, ESI, EDI, EBP))
 12887                              <1> 	;
 12888                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification : CF = 1
 12889                              <1> 	;              if i-number of the file is 0. (error)
 12890                              <1> 	;
 12891                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (06/10/2016)
 12892                              <1> 	;
 12893                              <1> 	; INPUT:
 12894                              <1> 	;	EAX = File Handle (File Descriptor, File Index)
 12895                              <1> 	;
 12896                              <1> 	; OUTPUT:
 12897                              <1> 	;	CF = 1 -> File not open !
 12898                              <1> 	;	CF = 0 -> OK!
 12899                              <1> 	;	     EBX = File Number (System)
 12900                              <1> 	;	     [cdev] = Logical DOS Drive Number
 12901                              <1> 	;	     EAX = File Handle/Number (user)
 12902                              <1> 	;
 12903                              <1> 	; Modified Registers: EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI, EDI, EBP

 13113                              <1> sysbreak:
 13114                              <1> 	; 06/09/2024 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.9
 13115                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
 13116                              <1> 	; 18/10/2015
 13117                              <1> 	; 07/10/2015
 13118                              <1> 	; 23/06/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
 13119                              <1> 	; 20/06/2013 - 24/03/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 13120                              <1> 	;
 13121                              <1> 	; 'sysbreak' sets the programs break points.
 13122                              <1> 	; It checks the current break point (u.break) to see if it is
 13123                              <1> 	; between "core" and the stack (sp). If it is, it is made an
 13124                              <1> 	; even address (if it was odd) and the area between u.break
 13125                              <1> 	; and the stack is cleared. The new breakpoint is then put
 13126                              <1> 	; in u.break and control is passed to 'sysret'.
 13127                              <1> 	;
 13128                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
 13129                              <1> 	;	sysbreak; addr
 13130                              <1> 	; Arguments: -
 13131                              <1> 	;
 13132                              <1> 	; Inputs: u.break - current breakpoint
 13133                              <1> 	; Outputs: u.break - new breakpoint 
 13134                              <1> 	;	area between old u.break and the stack (sp) is cleared.
 13135                              <1> 	;
 13136                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
 13137                              <1> 	; 06/09/2024 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.9 - Major Modification -
 13138                              <1> 	;
 13139                              <1> 	; 	This system call performs "malloc" function as in C.
 13140                              <1> 	; Input:
 13141                              <1> 	;    EBX = new u.break address (virtual, user's space)
 13142                              <1> 	; (Note: Default/Initial u.break address is the start of the BSS
 13143                              <1> 	;	 section. Or it is file size for PRG -flat image- files.)
 13144                              <1> 	; If EBX = 0FFFFFFFFh ; -1
 13145                              <1> 	;    Return current u.break in EAX
 13146                              <1> 	; Output:
 13147                              <1> 	;    If EBX input is -1, EAX = current u.break address (virtual)
 13148                              <1> 	;	otherwise, EAX = new u.break address
 13149                              <1> 	; Area between the new u.break and the old u.break is cleared.
 13150                              <1> 	; (Note: If the new break address cross overs user's esp,
 13151                              <1> 	;	 this area <new break - old break> is not cleared.)
 13152                              <1> 	; If CF=1 at return, it means Memory Allocation Error.
 13153                              <1> 	;		(or "Insufficient Memory" error)
 13154                              <1> 	;	EAX = 0
 13155                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
 13156                              <1> 	;
 13157                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification:
 13158                              <1> 	;	The user/application program puts breakpoint address
 13159                              <1> 	;       in BX register as 'sysbreak' system call argument.
 13160                              <1> 	; 	(argument transfer method 1)
 13161                              <1> 	;
 13162                              <1> 	;  NOTE: Beginning of core is 0 in Retro UNIX 8086 v1 !
 13163                              <1> 	; 	((!'sysbreak' is not needed in Retro UNIX 8086 v1!))
 13164                              <1> 	;  NOTE:
 13165                              <1> 	; 	'sysbreak' clears extended part (beyond of previous
 13166                              <1> 	;	'u.break' address) of user's memory for original unix's
 13167                              <1> 	;	'bss' compatibility with Retro UNIX 8086 v1 (19/11/2013)
 13168                              <1> 
 13169                              <1> 		; mov u.break,r1 / move users break point to r1
 13170                              <1> 		; cmp r1,$core / is it the same or lower than core?
 13171                              <1> 		; blos 1f / yes, 1f
 13172                              <1> 	; 23/06/2015
 13173 00011B73 8B2D[CCB00100]      <1> 	mov	ebp, [u.break] ; virtual address (offset)
