 13263                              <1> sysseek: ; / moves read write pointer in an fsp entry
 13264                              <1> 	; 27/12/2025 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10
 13265                              <1> 	; 06/11/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
 13266                              <1> 	; 22/06/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
 13267                              <1> 	; 07/07/2013 - 05/08/2013 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 13268                              <1> 	;
 13269                              <1> 	; 'sysseek' changes the r/w pointer of (3rd word of in an
 13270                              <1> 	; fsp entry) of an open file whose file descriptor is in u.r0.
 13271                              <1> 	; The file descriptor refers to a file open for reading or
 13272                              <1> 	; writing. The read (or write) pointer is set as follows:
 13273                              <1> 	;	* if 'ptrname' is 0, the pointer is set to offset.
 13274                              <1> 	;	* if 'ptrname' is 1, the pointer is set to its
 13275                              <1> 	;	  current location plus offset.
 13276                              <1> 	;	* if 'ptrname' is 2, the pointer is set to the
 13277                              <1> 	;	  size of file plus offset.
 13278                              <1> 	; The error bit (e-bit) is set for an undefined descriptor.
 13279                              <1> 	;
 13280                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
 13281                              <1> 	;	sysseek; offset; ptrname
 13282                              <1> 	; Arguments:
 13283                              <1> 	;	offset - number of bytes desired to move
 13284                              <1> 	;		 the r/w pointer
 13285                              <1> 	;	ptrname - a switch indicated above
 13286                              <1> 	;
 13287                              <1> 	; Inputs: r0 - file descriptor
 13288                              <1> 	;	; 27/12/2025
 13289                              <1> 	;	EBX = File descriptor (number) -user-
 13290                              <1> 	;	ECX = Offset (plus)
 13291                              <1> 	;	EDX = 0 -> set to offset in ECX
 13292                              <1> 	;	    = 1 -> set to current offset + offset in ECX
 13293                              <1> 	;	    = 2 -> set to file size + offset in ECX
 13294                              <1> 	; Outputs: -
 13295                              <1> 	;	EAX = (new) File Offset ; 27/12/2025
 13296                              <1> 	; ...............................................................
 13297                              <1> 	;
 13298                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification:
 13299                              <1> 	;       'sysseek' system call has three arguments; so,
 13300                              <1> 	;	* 1st argument, file descriptor is in BX (BL) register
 13301                              <1> 	;	* 2nd argument, offset is in CX register
 13302                              <1> 	;	* 3rd argument, ptrname/switch is in DX (DL) register
 13303                              <1> 
 13304 00011BE2 E823000000          <1> 	call	seektell
 13305                              <1> 	; EAX = Current R/W pointer of the file
 13306                              <1> 	; EBX = [u.fofp]
 13307                              <1> 	; [u.base] = offset (ECX input)

 13419                              <1> 	; 21/08/2024 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.9 modification

 13425                              <1> 	; routine. u.tty is checked if to see if a control tty exists.
 13426                              <1> 	; If one does the interrupt character in the tty buffer is
 13427                              <1> 	; cleared and 'sysret'is called. If one does not exits
 13428                              <1> 	; 'sysret' is just called.
 13429                              <1> 	;
 13430                              <1> 	; Calling sequence:
 13431                              <1> 	;	sysintr; arg
 13432                              <1> 	; Argument:
 13433                              <1> 	;	arg - if 0, interrupts (ASCII DELETE) are ignored.
 13434                              <1> 	;	    - if 1, interrupts cause their normal result
 13435                              <1> 	;		 i.e force an exit.
 13436                              <1> 	;	    - if arg is a location within the program,
 13437                              <1> 	;		control is passed to that location when
 13438                              <1> 	;		an interrupt occurs.
 13439                              <1> 	; Inputs: -
 13440                              <1> 	; Outputs: -

 13475                              <1> 	; 21/08/2024 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.9 modification
 13476                              <1> 	;	get/reset QUIT (u.quit) status

 13493                              <1> 	;		cease and a core image to be produced.

 13540                              <1> anyi: 
 13541                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022
 13542                              <1> 	; 06/10/2016 (TRDOS 386 = TRDOS v2.0)
 13543                              <1> 	; Major Modification!
 13544                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 does not permit to delete a file while it is open
 13545                              <1> 	; The role of 'anyi' procedure has beeen changed to ensure that.
 13546                              <1> 	; 
 13547                              <1> 	; 22/06/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1 - Beginning)
 13548                              <1> 	; 25/04/2013 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 13549                              <1> 	;
 13550                              <1> 	; 'anyi' is called if a file deleted while open.
 13551                              <1> 	; "anyi" checks to see if someone else has opened this file.
 13552                              <1> 	;
 13553                              <1> 	; INPUTS ->
 13554                              <1> 	;    r1 - contains an i-number
 13555                              <1> 	;    fsp - start of table containing open files
 13556                              <1> 	;
 13557                              <1> 	; OUTPUTS ->
 13558                              <1> 	;    "deleted" flag set in fsp entry of another occurrence of
 13559                              <1> 	;	   this file and r2 points 1st word of this fsp entry.
 13560                              <1> 	;    if file not found - bit in i-node map is cleared
 13561                              <1> 	;    			 (i-node is freed)
 13562                              <1> 	;               all blocks related to i-node are freed
 13563                              <1> 	;	        all flags in i-node are cleared
 13564                              <1> 	; ((AX = R1)) input
 13565                              <1> 	;
 13566                              <1> 	;    (Retro UNIX Prototype : 02/12/2012, UNIXCOPY.ASM)
 13567                              <1>         ;    ((Modified registers: EDX, ECX, EBX, ESI, EDI, EBP))
 13568                              <1> 	;
 13569                              <1> 	; / r1 contains an i-number
 13570                              <1> 
 13571                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (06/10/2016)
 13572                              <1> 	; 
 13573                              <1> 	; INPUT:
 13574                              <1> 	;	EAX = First Cluster
 13575                              <1> 	;	 DL = Logical DOS Drive Number
 13576                              <1> 	;
 13577                              <1> 	; OUTPUT:
 13578                              <1> 	;	CF = 1 -> EBX = File Handle/Number/Index
 13579                              <1> 	;	CF = 0 -> EBX = 0
 13580                              <1> 	;
 13581                              <1> 	; Modified Registers: EBX
 13582                              <1> 
 13583                              <1> 	xor	ebx, ebx
 13584                              <1> anyi_0: 
 13585                              <1> 	cmp	byte [ebx+OF_MODE], 0 ; 0 = empty entry
 13586                              <1> 	ja	short anyi_2 ; 1 (r), 2 (w) or 3 (r&w)
 13587                              <1> anyi_1:
 13588                              <1> 	inc	bl
 13589                              <1> 	cmp	bl, OPENFILES ; max. count of open files
 13590                              <1> 	jb	short anyi_0
 13591                              <1> 	xor	eax, eax
 13592                              <1> 	retn
 13593                              <1> anyi_2:
 13594                              <1> 	cmp	dl, [ebx+OF_DRIVE]
 13595                              <1> 	jne	short anyi_1
 13596                              <1> 	;shl	bx, 2 ; *4 (dword offset)
 13597                              <1> 	shl	ebx, 2 ; 23/07/2022
 13598                              <1> 	cmp	eax, [ebx+OF_FCLUSTER]
 13599                              <1> 	je	short anyi_3
 13600                              <1> 	;shr	bx, 2 ; /4 (byte offset)
 13601                              <1> 	shr	ebx, 2 ; 23/07/2022
 13602                              <1> 	jmp	short anyi_1
 13603                              <1> anyi_3:
 13604                              <1> 	;shr	bx, 2 ; /4 (bytes offset) (index)
 13605                              <1> 	shr	ebx, 2 ; 23/07/2022
 13606                              <1> 	stc
 13607                              <1> 	retn

 14572                              <1> tswitch: ; Retro UNIX 386 v1
 14573                              <1> tswap:
 14574                              <1> 	; 16/01/2017
 14575                              <1> 	; 21/05/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
 14576                              <1> 	; 10/05/2015 - 01/09/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1)
 14577                              <1> 	; 14/04/2013 - 14/02/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 14578                              <1> 	; time out swap, called when a user times out.
 14579                              <1> 	; the user is put on the low priority queue.
 14580                              <1> 	; This is done by making a link from the last user
 14581                              <1> 	; on the low priority queue to him via a call to 'putlu'.
 14582                              <1> 	; then he is swapped out.
 14583                              <1> 
 14584                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0) modification ->  ** 21/05/2016 **
 14585                              <1> 	;     * when a high priority (event) process will be stopped
 14586                              <1> 	;	(swapped out, swithched out/off), 'tswap/tswitch' will
 14587                              <1> 	;	not add it to a run queue.
 14588                              <1> 	;	/// What for: Process may be already in a run queue, 
 14589                              <1> 	;	it is unspeficied state because process might be started
 14590                              <1> 	;	by a timer event which does not regard previous priority
 14591                              <1> 	;	level and run queue of the process (for fast executing!).
 14592                              <1> 	;	After the 'run for event', process will be sequenced
 14593                              <1> 	;	to run by it's actual run queue. ///
 14594                              <1> 	;
 14595                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 386 v1 modification ->
 14596                              <1> 	;       swap (software task switch) is performed by changing
 14597                              <1> 	;	user's page directory (u.pgdir) instead of segment change
 14598                              <1> 	;	as in Retro UNIX 8086 v1.
 14599                              <1> 	;
 14600                              <1> 	; RETRO UNIX 8086 v1 modification ->
 14601                              <1> 	;       'swap to disk' is replaced with 'change running segment'
 14602                              <1> 	;	according to 8086 cpu (x86 real mode) architecture.
 14603                              <1> 	;	pdp-11 was using 64KB uniform memory while IBM PC
 14604                              <1> 	;	compatibles was using 1MB segmented memory
 14605                              <1> 	;	in 8086/8088 times.
 14606                              <1> 	;
 14607                              <1> 	; INPUTS ->
 14608                              <1> 	;    u.uno - users process number
 14609                              <1> 	;    runq+4 - lowest priority queue
 14610                              <1> 	; OUTPUTS ->
 14611                              <1> 	;    r0 - users process number
 14612                              <1> 	;    r2 - lowest priority queue address
 14613                              <1> 	;
 14614                              <1> 	; ((AX = R0, BX = R2)) output
 14615                              <1> 	; ((Modified registers: EDX, EBX, ECX, ESI, EDI))
 14616                              <1> 	;
 14617                              <1> 
 14618                              <1> 	NOTE:
 14619                              <1> 	;* [u.pri] priority level is specified by run queue which is process
 14620                              <1> 	;  comes to run from.
 14621                              <1> 	;* Initial [u.pri] is 1 ('normal/regular') for programs
 14622                              <1> 	;  (which are launched by MainProg or 'sysexec'), it is changed
 14623                              <1> 	;  to 2 ('high') by timer event, if program uses 'systimer' system call.
 14624                              <1> 	;* Program (Process) also can change it's running priority
 14625                              <1> 	;  from 1 to 0 or up to 2 by using 'syspri' system call; but,
 14626                              <1> 	;  if program selects priority level 2 (high) for running, next time
 14627                              <1> 	;  it is reduced to 1 (normal/regular) because 'syspri' adds this
 14628                              <1> 	;  program to 'run for normal' queue while running duration is a bit
 14629                              <1> 	;  protected from swap/switch out immediate, behalf of other high
 14630                              <1> 	;  priority process in sequence. Program (with high priority) will not
 14631                              <1> 	;  be swapped/switched out (by timer event) before it's time quantum
 14632                              <1> 	;  will be elapsed, but, this will be temporary if program is not using
 14633                              <1> 	;  timer event function.
 14634                              <1> 
 14635                              <1> 	;For example:
 14636                              <1> 	;If a process frequently gets a timer event, it runs at high priority
 14637                              <1> 	;level but when it returns from running it returns to actual run queue,
 14638                              <1> 	;not to 'run for event' queue again.
 14639                              <1> 	;'tswap' will not change the sequence at return/stop(swap out) stage.
 14640                              <1> 	;But if priority level not high (=2, 'run for event'), 'tswap/tswitch'
 14641                              <1> 	;will add the stopping process to relevant run queue according to
 14642                              <1> 	;[u.pri] priority level.
 14643                              <1> 
 14644                              <1> 	; 16/01/2017

 14671                              <1> 	; 20/08/2024
 14672                              <1> 	; 02/01/2017
 14673                              <1> 	; 21/05/2016
 14674                              <1> 	; 20/05/2016
 14675                              <1> 	; 02/05/2016

 14678                              <1> 	; 14/04/2013 - 08/03/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 14679                              <1> 	;
 14680                              <1> 	; 'swap' is routine that controls the swapping of processes
 14681                              <1> 	; in and out of core.
 14682                              <1> 	;
 14683                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0) modification ->  ** 20/05/2016 **
 14684                              <1> 	;     * 3 different priority level is applied
 14685                              <1> 	;	(just as original unix v1)
 14686                              <1> 	;	1) high priority (event) run queue, 'runq_event'
 14687                              <1> 	;	2) normal priority (regular) run queue, 'runq_normal'
 14688                              <1> 	;	3) low priority (background) run queue, 'runq_backgroud'
 14689                              <1> 	;	'swap' code will run a process which has max. priority
 14690                              <1>         ;       (for earliest event at first)
 14691                              <1> 	;
 14692                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 386 v1 modification ->
 14693                              <1> 	;       swap (software task switch) is performed by changing
 14694                              <1> 	;	user's page directory (u.pgdir) instead of segment change
 14695                              <1> 	;	as in Retro UNIX 8086 v1.
 14696                              <1> 	;
 14697                              <1> 	; RETRO UNIX 8086 v1 modification ->
 14698                              <1> 	;       'swap to disk' is replaced with 'change running segment'
 14699                              <1> 	;	according to 8086 cpu (x86 real mode) architecture.
 14700                              <1> 	;	pdp-11 was using 64KB uniform memory while IBM PC
 14701                              <1> 	;	compatibles was using 1MB segmented memory
 14702                              <1> 	;	in 8086/8088 times.
 14703                              <1> 	;
 14704                              <1> 	; INPUTS ->
 14705                              <1> 	;    runq table - contains processes to run.
 14706                              <1> 	;    p.link - contains next process in line to be run.
 14707                              <1> 	;    u.uno - process number of process in core
 14708                              <1> 	;    s.stack - swap stack used as an internal stack for swapping.
 14709                              <1> 	; OUTPUTS ->
 14710                              <1> 	;    (original unix v1 -> present process to its disk block)
 14711                              <1> 	;    (original unix v1 -> new process into core -> 
 14712                              <1> 	;	   Retro Unix 8086 v1 -> segment registers changed
 14713                              <1> 	;	   for new process)
 14714                              <1> 	;    u.quant = 3 (Time quantum for a process)
 14715                              <1> 	; 	((INT 1Ch count down speed -> 18.2 times per second)
 14716                              <1> 	;    RETRO UNIX 8086 v1 will use INT 1Ch (18.2 times per second)
 14717                              <1> 	;	 for now, it will swap the process if there is not
 14718                              <1> 	;	 a keyboard event (keystroke) (Int 15h, function 4Fh)
 14719                              <1> 	;	 or will count down from 3 to 0 even if there is a
 14720                              <1> 	;        keyboard event locking due to repetitive key strokes.
 14721                              <1> 	;	 u.quant will be reset to 3 for RETRO UNIX 8086 v1.
 14722                              <1> 	;
 14723                              <1> 	; ((Modified registers: EAX, EDX, EBX, ECX, ESI, EDI))
 14724                              <1> 
 14725                              <1> 	;NOTE:
 14726                              <1> 	;High priority queue is the first for selecting a process to run.
 14727                              <1> 	;If there is not a process in high priority level run queue,
 14728                              <1> 	;a process in normal priority run queue will be selected
 14729                              <1> 	;or a proces in low priority run queue will be selected if normal
 14730                              <1> 	;priority level run queue is empty.

 14806                              <1> wswap:  ; < swap out, swap to disk >
 14807                              <1> 	; 28/02/2017 (fnsave)
 14808                              <1> 	; 29/04/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
 14809                              <1> 	; 09/05/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1)
 14810                              <1> 	; 26/05/2013 - 08/03/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 14811                              <1> 	; 'wswap' writes out the process that is in core onto its
 14812                              <1> 	; appropriate disk area.
 14813                              <1> 	;
 14814                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 386 v1 modification ->
 14815                              <1> 	;       User (u) structure content and the user's register content
 14816                              <1> 	;	will be copied to the process's/user's UPAGE (a page for
 14817                              <1> 	;	saving 'u' structure and user registers for task switching).
 14818                              <1> 	;	u.usp - points to kernel stack address which contains
 14819                              <1> 	;		user's registers while entering system call.
 14820                              <1> 	;	u.sp  - points to kernel stack address
 14821                              <1> 	;		to return from system call -for IRET-.
 14822                              <1> 	;	[u.usp]+32+16 = [u.sp] 
 14823                              <1> 	;	[u.usp] -> edi, esi, ebp, esp (= [u.usp]+32), ebx,
 14824                              <1> 	;		edx, ecx, eax, gs, fs, es, ds, -> [u.sp].
 14825                              <1> 	;
 14826                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 8086 v1 modification ->
 14827                              <1> 	;       'swap to disk' is replaced with 'change running segment'
 14828                              <1> 	;	according to 8086 cpu (x86 real mode) architecture.
 14829                              <1> 	;	pdp-11 was using 64KB uniform memory while IBM PC
 14830                              <1> 	;	compatibles was using 1MB segmented memory 
 14831                              <1> 	;	in 8086/8088 times.
 14832                              <1> 	;
 14833                              <1> 	; INPUTS ->
 14834                              <1> 	;    u.break - points to end of program
 14835                              <1> 	;    u.usp - stack pointer at the moment of swap
 14836                              <1> 	;    core - beginning of process program
 14837                              <1> 	;    ecore - end of core
 14838                              <1> 	;    user - start of user parameter area
 14839                              <1> 	;    u.uno - user process number
 14840                              <1> 	;    p.dska - holds block number of process
 14841                              <1> 	; OUTPUTS ->
 14842                              <1> 	;    swp I/O queue
 14843                              <1> 	;    p.break - negative word count of process
 14844                              <1> 	;    r1 - process disk address
 14845                              <1> 	;    r2 - negative word count
 14846                              <1> 	;
 14847                              <1> 	; RETRO UNIX 8086 v1 input/output:
 14848                              <1> 	;
 14849                              <1> 	; INPUTS ->
 14850                              <1> 	;    u.uno - process number (to be swapped out)
 14851                              <1> 	; OUTPUTS ->

 14885                              <1> rswap:  ; < swap in, swap from disk >
 14886                              <1> 	; 28/02/2017 (frstor)
 14887                              <1> 	; 15/01/2017
 14888                              <1> 	; 14/01/2017
 14889                              <1> 	; 21/05/2016
 14890                              <1> 	; 03/05/2016
 14891                              <1> 	; 29/04/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
 14892                              <1> 	; 09/05/2015 - 15/09/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1)
 14893                              <1> 	; 26/05/2013 - 08/03/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 14894                              <1> 	; 'rswap' reads a process whose number is in r1,
 14895                              <1> 	; from disk into core.
 14896                              <1> 	;
 14897                              <1> 	; Retro UNIX 386 v1 modification ->
 14898                              <1> 	;       User (u) structure content and the user's register content
 14899                              <1> 	;	will be restored from process's/user's UPAGE (a page for
 14900                              <1> 	;	saving 'u' structure and user registers for task switching).
 14901                              <1> 	;	u.usp - points to kernel stack address which contains
 14902                              <1> 	;		user's registers while entering system call.
 14903                              <1> 	;	u.sp  - points to kernel stack address
 14904                              <1> 	;		to return from system call -for IRET-.
 14905                              <1> 	;	[u.usp]+32+16 = [u.sp]
 14906                              <1> 	;	[u.usp] -> edi, esi, ebp, esp (= [u.usp]+32), ebx,
 14907                              <1> 	;		edx, ecx, eax, gs, fs, es, ds, -> [u.sp].
 14908                              <1> 	;
 14909                              <1> 	; RETRO UNIX 8086 v1 modification ->
 14910                              <1> 	;       'swap to disk' is replaced with 'change running segment'
 14911                              <1> 	;	according to 8086 cpu (x86 real mode) architecture.
 14912                              <1> 	;	pdp-11 was using 64KB uniform memory while IBM PC
 14913                              <1> 	;	compatibles was using 1MB segmented memory
 14914                              <1> 	;	in 8086/8088 times.
 14915                              <1> 	;
 14916                              <1> 	; INPUTS ->
 14917                              <1> 	;    r1 - process number of process to be read in
 14918                              <1> 	;    p.break - negative of word count of process
 14919                              <1> 	;    p.dska - disk address of the process
 14920                              <1> 	;    u.emt - determines handling of emt's
 14921                              <1> 	;    u.ilgins - determines handling of illegal instructions
 14922                              <1> 	; OUTPUTS ->
 14923                              <1> 	;    8 = (u.ilgins)
 14924                              <1> 	;    24 = (u.emt)
 14925                              <1> 	;    swp - bit 10 is set to indicate read
 14926                              <1> 	;		(bit 15=0 when reading is done)
 14927                              <1> 	;    swp+2 - disk block address
 14928                              <1> 	;    swp+4 - negative word count
 14929                              <1> 	;      ((swp+6 - address of user structure))
 14930                              <1> 	;
 14931                              <1> 	; RETRO UNIX 8086 v1 input/output:
 14932                              <1> 	;

 14935                              <1> 	; OUTPUTS ->
 14936                              <1> 	;    none
 14937                              <1> 	;
 14938                              <1> 	;   ((Modified registers: EAX, ECX, ESI, EDI, ESP))

 14976                              <1> putlu: 
 14977                              <1> 	; 20/05/2016
 14978                              <1> 	; 29/04/2016 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
 14979                              <1> 	; 10/05/2015 - 12/09/2015 (Retro UNIX 386 v1)
 14980                              <1> 	; 15/04/2013 - 23/02/2014 (Retro UNIX 8086 v1)
 14981                              <1> 	; 'putlu' is called with a process number in r1 and a pointer
 14982                              <1> 	; to lowest priority Q (runq+4) in r2. A link is created from
 14983                              <1> 	; the last process on the queue to process in r1 by putting
 14984                              <1> 	; the process number in r1 into the last process's link.
 14985                              <1> 	;
 14986                              <1> 	; INPUTS ->
 14987                              <1> 	;    r1 - user process number
 14988                              <1> 	;    r2 - points to lowest priority queue
 14989                              <1> 	;    p.dska - disk address of the process
 14990                              <1> 	;    u.emt - determines handling of emt's
 14991                              <1> 	;    u.ilgins - determines handling of illegal instructions

 14993                              <1> 	;    r3 - process number of last process on the queue upon
 14994                              <1> 	;	  entering putlu
 14995                              <1> 	;    p.link-1 + r3 - process number in r1
 14996                              <1> 	;    r2 - points to lowest priority queue
 14997                              <1> 	;
 14998                              <1> 	; ((Modified registers: EDX, EBX))
 14999                              <1> 	;

 15001                              <1>

 15003                              <1> 	; EAX = r1 (AL=r1b)
 15004                              <1>

 15007                              <1> 	;     (max. 16 processes available for current kernel version)
 15008                              <1> 	; EBX = run queue address ; 20/05/2016 (TRDOS 386)
 15009                              <1> 		; which is one of following addresses:
 15010                              <1> 		;  1) 'runq_event' high priority run queue
 15011                              <1> 		;  2) 'runq_normal' normal/regular priority run queue
 15012                              <1> 		;  3) 'runq_background' low priority run queue

 15048                              <1> syspri: ; change running priority (of the process)
 15049                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
 15050                              <1> 	; 21/05/2016
 15051                              <1> 	; 20/05/2026 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
 15052                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
 15053                              <1> 	;	BL = priority level
 15054                              <1> 	;	   0 = low running priority (running on background)
 15055                              <1> 	;	   1 = normal/regular priority (running as regular)
 15056                              <1> 	;	   2 = high/event priority (running for event)
 15057                              <1> 	;	   >2 = invalid, it will accepted as 2 (event)
 15058                              <1> 	;	   0FFh = get/return current running priority only
 15059                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
 15060                              <1> 	;	* if current [u.pri] < 2
 15061                              <1> 	;	  if BL input < 0FFh ->
 15062                              <1> 	;	     [u.pri] is updated as in BL input (0,1,2)
 15063                              <1> 	;	  if BL input = 0FFh -> AL = [u.pri] (current)
 15064                              <1> 	;
 15065                              <1> 	;	* if current [u.pri] = 2
 15066                              <1> 	;	  if BL input < 0FFh -> cf = 1 & AL = 2
 15067                              <1> 	;	  if BL input = 0FFh -> cf = 0 & AL = 2
 15068                              <1> 	;
 15069                              <1> 	;	NOTE:
 15070                              <1> 	;	If [u.pri] = 2, it can not be changed to 1 or 0;
 15071                              <1> 	;	because, run queue of the running process is unspecified
 15072                              <1> 	;	at this	stage. Process might be started by a timer event
 15073                              <1> 	;	or priority might be changed to high by previous
 15074                              <1> 	;	'syspri' system	call. In both cases, the process is in
 15075                              <1> 	;	'runq_normal' or 'runq_background' queue.
 15076                              <1> 	;	As result of this fact, when the [u.quant] time quantum
 15077                              <1> 	;	of the process is elapsed or 'sysrele' system call is
 15078                              <1> 	;	instructed by the process, 'tswap' ('tswitch') procedure
 15079                              <1> 	;	will be called (to 'swap' or 'switch' out the procedure)
 15080                              <1> 	;	and it will not call 'putlu' to add the (stopping)
 15081                              <1> 	;	process to relevant run queue when [u.pri] = 2.
 15082                              <1> 	;	(Otherwise, it would be possible to add process to
 15083                              <1> 	;	a run queue while it is already in a run queue, wrongly.)
 15084                              <1>   	;
 15085                              <1> 	;	If [u.pri]< 2, 'tswap/tswitch' procedure will call
 15086                              <1> 	;	'putlu' to add process to relevant run queue
 15087                              <1> 	;	according to [u.pri] value. ('runq_normal' for 1,
 15088                              <1> 	;	'runq_background' for 0).
 15089                              <1> 	;
 15090                              <1> 	;	If BL input >= 2 and < 0FFh while [u.pri] < 2,
 15091                              <1> 	;	process will be added to 'runq_normal' queue and
 15092                              <1> 	;	[u.pri] will be set to 2. (in 'syspri' system call)
 15093                              <1> 	;
 15094                              <1>

 15337                              <1> sysfff: ; <Find First File>
 15338                              <1> 	; 25/05/2025
 15339                              <1> 	; 18/05/2025 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.10) ((v2.1.0))
 15340                              <1> 	; 25/08/2024 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.9)
 15341                              <1> 	; 08/08/2022
 15342                              <1> 	; 30/07/2022 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5)
 15343                              <1> 	; 17/10/2016
 15344                              <1> 	; 16/10/2016
 15345                              <1> 	; 15/10/2016 TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0) feature only !
 15346                              <1> 	;           -derived from TRDOS v1.0, INT_21H.ASM-
 15347                              <1> 	;            ("loc_INT21h_find_first_file")
 15348                              <1> 	; TRDOS 8086 (v1.0)
 15349                              <1>         ; 	07/08/2011
 15350                              <1>         ;	Find First File
 15351                              <1> 	;	INPUT:
 15352                              <1>         ;	    CX= Attributes
 15353                              <1>         ;	    DS:DX= Pointer to filename
 15354                              <1> 	;	MSDOS OUTPUT:
 15355                              <1> 	;	    DTA: (Default address: PSP offset 80h)
 15356                              <1> 	;	    Offset  Descrription
 15357                              <1> 	;	    0	    Reserved for use find next file
 15358                              <1> 	;	    21	    Attribute of file found
 15359                              <1> 	;	    22	    Time stamp of file
 15360                              <1> 	;	    24	    Date stamp of file
 15361                              <1> 	;	    26	    File size in bytes
 15362                              <1> 	;	    30	    Filename and extension (zero terminated)
 15363                              <1> 	;	If cf = 1:
 15364                              <1> 	;	    Error Codes: (in AX)
 15365                              <1> 	;	    	2 - File not found
 15366                              <1> 	;	       18 - No more files
 15367                              <1>         ;
 15368                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (v2.0)
 15369                              <1> 	; 15/10/2016
 15370                              <1> 	;
 15371                              <1>         ; INPUT ->
 15372                              <1>         ;	   CL = File attributes
 15373                              <1> 	;     	      bit 0 (1) - Read only file (R)
 15374                              <1> 	;             bit 1 (1) - Hidden file (H)
 15375                              <1>         ;             bit 2 (1) - System file (R)
 15376                              <1> 	;             bit 3 (1) - Volume label/name (V)
 15377                              <1>         ;             bit 4 (1) - Subdirectory (D)
 15378                              <1> 	;	      bit 5 (1) - File has been archived (A)
 15379                              <1> 	;	   CH = 0 -> Return basic parameters (24 bytes)
 15380                              <1> 	;	   CH > 0 -> Return FindFile structure/table (128 bytes)
 15381                              <1>         ;          EBX = Pointer to filename (ASCIIZ) -path-
 15382                              <1> 	;	   EDX = File parameters buffer address
 15383                              <1> 	;		(buffer size = 24 bytes if CH input = 0)
 15384                              <1> 	;		(buffer size = 128 bytes if CH input > 0)
 15385                              <1> 	;
 15386                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
 15387                              <1> 	;	   EAX = 0 if CH input > 0
 15388                              <1> 	;	   EAX = First cluster number of file if CH input = 0
 15389                              <1> 	;	   EDX = File parameters table/structure address
 15390                              <1> 	;	   Basic Parameters:
 15391                              <1> 	;		Offset  Description
 15392                              <1> 	;		------	---------------
 15393                              <1> 	;		0	File Attributes
 15394                              <1> 	;		1	Ambiguous filename chars are used sign
 15395                              <1> 	;			(0 = filename fits exactly with request)
 15396                              <1> 	;			(>0 = ambiguous filename chars are used)
 15397                              <1> 	;	      	2	Time stamp of file
 15398                              <1> 	;		4	Date stamp of file
 15399                              <1> 	;		6	File size in bytes
 15400                              <1> 	;		10	Short Filename (ASCIIZ, max. 13 bytes)
 15401                              <1> 	;		23	Longname Length (1-255) if existing
 15402                              <1> 	;
 15403                              <1> 	;          cf = 1 -> Error code in AL
 15404                              <1> 	;
 15405                              <1> 	; Modified Registers: EAX (at the return of system call)
 15406                              <1> 	;
 15407                              <1> 	; TR-DOS FindFile (FFF) Structure (128 bytes):
 15408                              <1> 	; 09/10/2011 (DIR.ASM) - 10/02/2016 (trdoskx.s)
 15409                              <1> 	;
 15410                              <1> 	; Offset   Parameter			Size
 15411                              <1> 	; ------   ------------------		--------
 15412                              <1> 	; 0	   FindFile_Drv			1 byte
 15413                              <1> 	; 1	   FindFile_Directory		65 bytes
 15414                              <1> 	; 66	   FindFile_Name		13 bytes
 15415                              <1> 	; 79	   FindFile_LongNameEntryLength 1 byte
 15416                              <1> 	;Above 80 bytes form
 15417                              <1> 	;TR-DOS Source/Destination File FullName Format/Structure
 15418                              <1> 	; 80	   FindFile_AttributesMask	1 word
 15419                              <1> 	; 82	   FindFile_DirEntry		32 bytes (*)
 15420                              <1> 	; 114	   FindFile_DirFirstCluster	1 double word
 15421                              <1> 	; 118	   FindFile_DirCluster		1 double word
 15422                              <1> 	; 122	   FindFile_DirEntryNumber	1 word
 15423                              <1> 	; 124	   FindFile_MatchCounter	1 word
 15424                              <1> 	; 126	   FindFile_Reserved		1 word
 15425                              <1>    	; (*) MS-DOS, FAT 12-16-32 classic directory entry (32 bytes)
 15426                              <1> 	;
 15427                              <1> 	; ***********************************************************
 15428                              <1> 	;
 15429                              <1> 	; 18/05/2025 (Major Modification)
 15430                              <1> 	; ------ TR-DOS 386 v2.0.10 --------
 15431                              <1> 	; FindFile - SysFFF/SysFNF Structure (<=281 bytes):
 15432                              <1> 	;
 15433                              <1> 	; Offset   Parameter			Size
 15434                              <1> 	; ------   ------------------		--------
 15435                              <1> 	; 0	   FindFile_DirEntry		32 bytes (*)
 15436                              <1> 	; 32	   FindFile_Drv			1 byte
 15437                              <1> 	; 33	   FindFile_Directory		65 bytes (104 bytes)
 15438                              <1> 	; 98	   FindFile_Name		13 bytes
 15439                              <1> 	; 111	   FindFile_LongNameEntryLength 1 byte
 15440                              <1> 	; 112	   FindFile_Longname		129 bytes (max.) (**)
 15441                              <1> 	;
 15442                              <1> 	; Parameters table/structure size: max. 280 bytes (**)
 15443                              <1> 	;
 15444                              <1> 	;		; 25/05/2025 (**)
 15445                              <1> 	; Return Options:
 15446                              <1> 	;	CH = 0 -> basic (24 bytes)
 15447                              <1> 	;	CH bits
 15448                              <1> 	;	   bit 0 - FindFile_DirEntry
 15449                              <1> 	;	   bit 1 - FindFile_Drv
 15450                              <1> 	;	   bit 2 - FindFile_Directory (65 bytes)
 15451                              <1> 	;	   bit 3 - FindFile_Name
 15452                              <1> 	;	   bit 4 - FindFile_LongNameEntryLength
 15453                              <1> 	;	   bit 5 - FindFile_Longname (65 bytes) (ASCIIZ)
 15454                              <1> 	;	   bit 6 - use 104 bytes buf for directory
 15455                              <1> 	;	   bit 7 - use 128+1 bytes buf for longname (**)
 15456                              <1> 	; 	examples:
 15457                              <1> 	;	  1Fh -	00011111b needs 112 bytes buffer
 15458                              <1> 	;	  0Fh -	01001111b needs 150 bytes buffer
 15459                              <1> 	;	 0EFh -	11101111b needs 279 bytes buffer
 15460                              <1> 	;	 0FFh -	11111111b needs 280 bytes buffer (**)
 15461                              <1> 	;	 07Fh - 01111111b needs 216 bytes buffer (**)
 15462                              <1> 	;	 03Fh - 00111111b needs 177 bytes buffer (**)
 15463                              <1> 	;
 15464                              <1> 	; (**) ASCIIZ (not UNICODE) long name (max. 128+NUL bytes)
 15465                              <1> 	;
 15466                              <1> 	; Note:
 15467                              <1> 	;	if EDX input is 0
 15468                              <1> 	;		Only File Size will be returned in EAX (*)
 15469                              <1> 	;	if CH > 0 but
 15470                              <1> 	;	   CH & 3Fh is 0, buffer will not used (*)
 15471                              <1> 	;
 15472                              <1> 	; ***********************************************************
 15473                              <1> 	;
 15474                              <1> 
 15475                              <1> 	;mov	[u.namep], ebx

 15877                              <1> sysfnf: ; <Find Next File>
 15878                              <1> 	; 25/05/2025
 15879                              <1> 	; 19/05/2025
 15880                              <1> 	; 18/05/2025 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.10) ((v2.1.0))
 15881                              <1> 	; 25/08/2024 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.9)
 15882                              <1> 	; 29/08/2023 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.6)
 15883                              <1> 	; 08/08/2022
 15884                              <1> 	; 30/07/2022 (TRDOS 386 Kernel v2.0.5)
 15885                              <1> 	; 16/10/2016 TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0) feature only !
 15886                              <1> 	;           -derived from TRDOS v1.0, INT_21H.ASM-
 15887                              <1> 	;            ("loc_INT21h_find_next_file")
 15888                              <1> 	; TRDOS 8086 (v1.0)
 15889                              <1>         ; 	07/08/2011 
 15890                              <1>         ;	Find First File
 15891                              <1> 	;	INPUT:
 15892                              <1>         ;	    none
 15893                              <1> 	;	MSDOS OUTPUT:
 15894                              <1> 	;	    DTA: (Default address: PSP offset 80h)
 15895                              <1> 	;	    Offset  Descrription
 15896                              <1> 	;	    0	    Reserved for use find next file
 15897                              <1> 	;	    21	    Attribute of file found
 15898                              <1> 	;	    22	    Time stamp of file
 15899                              <1> 	;	    24	    Date stamp of file
 15900                              <1> 	;	    26	    File size in bytes
 15901                              <1> 	;	    30	    Filename and extension (zero terminated)
 15902                              <1> 	;	If cf = 1:
 15903                              <1> 	;	    Error Codes: (in AX)
 15904                              <1> 	;	       18 - No more files
 15905                              <1>         ;
 15906                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 (v2.0)
 15907                              <1> 	; 16/10/2016
 15908                              <1> 	;
 15909                              <1>         ; INPUT ->
 15910                              <1>        	; 	   none
 15911                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
 15912                              <1> 	;	   EAX = 0 if CH input of 'Find First File' > 0
 15913                              <1> 	;	   EAX = First cluster number of file
 15914                              <1> 	;		 if CH input of 'Find First File' = 0
 15915                              <1> 	;	   EDX = File parameters table/structure address
 15916                              <1> 	;
 15917                              <1> 	;          cf = 1 -> Error code in AL
 15918                              <1> 	;
 15919                              <1>  	; Modified Registers: EAX (at the return of system call)
 15920                              <1> 	;
 15921                              <1> 	; Note: If byte [FFF_Valid] = 0
 15922                              <1> 	;	'sysfnf' will return with 'no more files' error.
 15923                              <1> 	;	If byte [FFF_Valid] = 24
 15924                              <1> 	;	'sysfnf' will return with 24 bytes basic parameters
 15925                              <1> 	;	at the address which is in EDX.
 15926                              <1> 	;	If byte [FFF_Valid] = 128
 15927                              <1> 	;	'sysfnf' will return with 128 bytes Find File
 15928                              <1> 	;	Structure/Table at the address which is in EDX.
 15929                              <1> 	;
 15930                              <1> 	; ***********************************************************
 15931                              <1> 	;
 15932                              <1> 	; 18/05/2025 (Major Modification)
 15933                              <1> 	; ------ TR-DOS 386 v2.0.10 --------
 15934                              <1> 	; FindFile - SysFFF/SysFNF Structure (<=281 bytes):
 15935                              <1> 	;
 15936                              <1> 	; Offset   Parameter			Size
 15937                              <1> 	; ------   ------------------		--------
 15938                              <1> 	; 0	   FindFile_DirEntry		32 bytes (*)
 15939                              <1> 	; 32	   FindFile_Drv			1 byte
 15940                              <1> 	; 33	   FindFile_Directory		65 bytes (104 bytes)
 15941                              <1> 	; 98	   FindFile_Name		13 bytes
 15942                              <1> 	; 111	   FindFile_LongNameEntryLength 1 byte
 15943                              <1> 	; 112	   FindFile_Longname		129 bytes (max.) (**)
 15944                              <1> 	;
 15945                              <1> 	; Parameters table/structure size: max. 280 bytes (**)
 15946                              <1> 	;
 15947                              <1> 	;		; 25/05/2025 (**)
 15948                              <1> 	; Return Options:
 15949                              <1> 	;	CH = 0 -> basic (24 bytes)
 15950                              <1> 	;	CH bits
 15951                              <1> 	;	   bit 0 - FindFile_DirEntry
 15952                              <1> 	;	   bit 1 - FindFile_Drv
 15953                              <1> 	;	   bit 2 - FindFile_Directory (65 bytes)
 15954                              <1> 	;	   bit 3 - FindFile_Name
 15955                              <1> 	;	   bit 4 - FindFile_LongNameEntryLength
 15956                              <1> 	;	   bit 5 - FindFile_Longname (65 bytes) (ASCIIZ)
 15957                              <1> 	;	   bit 6 - use 104 bytes buf for directory
 15958                              <1> 	;	   bit 7 - use 128+1 bytes buf for longname (**)
 15959                              <1> 	; 	examples:

 17492                              <1> sysalloc:
 17493                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
 17494                              <1> 	; 14/10/2017
 17495                              <1> 	; 20/08/2017 - 01/09/2017
 17496                              <1> 	; 20/02/2017 - 04/03/2017 - 15/05/2017
 17497                              <1> 	; 19/02/2017 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
 17498                              <1> 	; (TRDOS 386 feature only!)
 17499                              <1> 	;
 17500                              <1> 	; Allocate Contiguous Memory Block/Pages (for user)
 17501                              <1> 	; (System call for DMA Buffer allocation etc.)
 17502                              <1> 	;
 17503                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
 17504                              <1> 	;	EBX = Virtual address (for user)
 17505                              <1> 	;	     (Physical memory block/aperture
 17506                              <1> 	;	     will be mapped to this virtual address)
 17507                              <1> 	;	ECX = Byte Count
 17508                              <1> 	;	     (will be rounded up to page border)
 17509                              <1> 	;	If ECX = 0
 17510                              <1> 	;	    System call will return with an error (cf=1)
 17511                              <1> 	;	    but ECX will contain maximum size of
 17512                              <1> 	;	    available memory aperture and physical
 17513                              <1> 	;	    (beginning) address of that aperture
 17514                              <1> 	;	    (which have maximum size) will be in EAX.
 17515                              <1> 	;	EDX = Upper limit of the requested physical memory
 17516                              <1> 	;	      block/pages.
 17517                              <1> 	;	     (The last byte address of the memory aperture
 17518                              <1> 	;	      must not be equal to or above this limit.)
 17519                              <1> 	;	If EDX = 0
 17520                              <1> 	; 	   there is NOLIMIT !
 17521                              <1> 	;	If EDX = 0FFFFFFFFh (-1)
 17522                              <1> 	;	   ESI = Lower Limit !
 17523                              <1> 	;		(Beginning of the block must not be 'less'
 17524                              <1> 	;		than this.) (Must be equal to or above...)
 17525                              <1> 	;	   EDI = Upper Limit !
 17526                              <1> 	;		(End of the block must be !less! than this)
 17527                              <1> 	;		(The last byte addr of the memory aperture
 17528                              <1> 	;		must not be equal to or above this limit.)
 17529                              <1> 	;
 17530                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
 17531                              <1> 	;	If CF = 0
 17532                              <1> 	;	EAX = Physical address of the allocated memory block
 17533                              <1> 	;	ECX = Allocated bytes (as rounded up to page borders)
 17534                              <1> 	;	EBX = Virtual address (as rounded up)
 17535                              <1> 	;	IF CF = 1
 17536                              <1> 	;	    Requested (size of) Memory block could not be
 17537                              <1> 	;	    allocated to the user!
 17538                              <1> 	;	IF CF = 1 & EAX = 0 (Insufficient memory error!)
 17539                              <1> 	;	   ECX = Total number of free bytes
 17540                              <1> 	;	         (not size of available contiguous bytes!)
 17541                              <1> 	;	If CF = 1 & EAX > 0
 17542                              <1> 	;	   there is not a memory aperture with requested size
 17543                              <1> 	;	   but total free mem is not less than requested size.
 17544                              <1> 	;	   EAX = Physical addr of available memory aperture
 17545                              <1> 	;	   	 with max size 
 17546                              <1> 	;	        (but it doesn't fit to the conditions!)
 17547                              <1> 	;	   ECX = Size of available memory aperture in bytes.
 17548                              <1> 	;	If CF = 1 -> EAX = 0FFFFFFFFh
 17549                              <1> 	;	   Conditions/Parameters are wrong !
 17550                              <1> 	;	   ECX is same with input value.
 17551                              <1> 	;
 17552                              <1> 	; Note:	Previously allocated pages will be deallocated if
 17553                              <1> 	;       new allocation conditions are met.

 17672                              <1> sysdalloc:
 17673                              <1> 	; 19/02/2017 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
 17674                              <1> 	; (TRDOS 386 feature only!)
 17675                              <1> 	;
 17676                              <1> 	; Deallocate Memory Block/Pages (for user)
 17677                              <1> 	; (Complementary call for sysalloc.)
 17678                              <1> 	;
 17679                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
 17680                              <1> 	;	EBX = Virtual address (for user)
 17681                              <1> 	;	      (will be rounded up to page border)
 17682                              <1> 	;	ECX = Byte Count
 17683                              <1> 	;	     (will be adjusted to page borders)
 17684                              <1> 	;	If ICX = 0
 17685                              <1> 	;	   nothing to do
 17686                              <1> 	;	If EBX + ECX > User's ESP
 17687                              <1> 	;	   nothing to do
 17688                              <1> 	;
 17689                              <1> 	; Note: u.break control may be included in future versions
 17690                              <1> 	;
 17691                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
 17692                              <1> 	;	If CF = 0
 17693                              <1> 	;	   EAX = Deallocated memory bytes
 17694                              <1> 	;	   EBX = Virtual address (as rounded up)
 17695                              <1> 	;	IF CF = 1
 17696                              <1> 	;	   EAX = 0
 17697                              <1> 	;
 17698                              <1> 	; Note:	Main purpose of this call is to deallocate/release
 17699                              <1> 	;	previously allocated (physically) contiguous memory
 17700                              <1> 	;	pages but beginning (virtual) address may not be
 17701                              <1> 	;	followed by physically contiguous pages. So, this
 17702                              <1> 	;	system call will deallocate user's virtually
 17703                              <1> 	;	contiguous memory pages. Also, there is not any
 17704                              <1> 	;	objections to use this system call without sysalloc
 17705                              <1> 	;	system call; only possible objection is to lost data
 17706                              <1> 	;	within user's memory space, if the beginning address
 17707                              <1> 	;	and size is not proper.
 17708                              <1> 	;
 17709                              <1> 	; Note: Empty page tables will not be deallocated!!!
 17710                              <1> 	;       (they will be deallocated at process termination)
 17711                              <1> 	;
 17712                              <1> 	; Note: When the program terminates itself or when it is 
 17713                              <1> 	;	terminated by operating system kernel, all allocated
 17714                              <1> 	;	memory pages will be deallocated during termination
 17715                              <1> 	;	stage. So, 'sysdalloc' is not necessary except 
 17716                              <1> 	;	forgiving memory block to other programs/processes.
 17717                              <1> 	;
 17718 00012A65 8B15[9CB00100]      <1> 	mov	edx, [u.sp]
 17719 00012A6B 8B420C              <1> 	mov	eax, [edx+12] ; user's stack pointer
 17720 00012A6E 29C8                <1> 	sub	eax, ecx ; esp - byte count
 17721 00012A70 24FC                <1> 	and	al, 0FCh ; dword alignment
 17722 00012A72 39D8                <1> 	cmp	eax, ebx
 17723 00012A74 7220                <1> 	jb	short sysdalloc_err ; deallocation overlaps with stack
 17724                              <1>

 17728                              <1>

 17742                              <1> syscalbac:
 17743                              <1> 	; SYS CALLBACK
 17744                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
 17745                              <1> 	; 03/08/2020
 17746                              <1> 	; 16/04/2017
 17747                              <1> 	; 14/04/2017
 17748                              <1> 	; 13/04/2017
 17749                              <1> 	; 28/02/2017
 17750                              <1> 	; 26/02/2017
 17751                              <1> 	; 24/02/2017
 17752                              <1> 	; 21/02/2017 - TRDOS 386 (TRDOS v2.0)
 17753                              <1> 	; (TRDOS 386 feature only!)
 17754                              <1> 	;
 17755                              <1> 	; Link or unlink IRQ callback service to/from user (ring 3)
 17756                              <1> 	;
 17757                              <1> 	; INPUT ->
 17758                              <1> 	;	BL = IRQ number (Hardware interrupt request number)
 17759                              <1> 	;	     (0 t0 15 but IRQ 0,1,2,6,8,14,15 are prohibited)
 17760                              <1> 	;	     IRQ numbers 3,4,5,7,9,10,11,12,13 are valid
 17761                              <1> 	;	     (numbers >15 are invalid)
 17762                              <1> 	;
 17763                              <1> 	;	BH = 0 = Unlink IRQ (in BL) from user (ring 3) service
 17764                              <1> 	;	     1 = Link IRQ by using Signal Response Byte method
 17765                              <1> 	;	     2 = Link IRQ by using Callback service method
 17766                              <1> 	;	     3 = Link IRQ by using Auto Increment S.R.B. method
 17767                              <1> 	;	    >3 = invalid 
 17768                              <1> 	;
 17769                              <1> 	;	CL = Signal Return/Response Byte value
 17770                              <1> 	;
 17771                              <1> 	;	If BH = 3, kernel will put a counter value  ; 03/08/2020
 17772                              <1> 	;	          (into the S.R.B. addr)
 17773                              <1> 	;		  between 0 to 255. (start value = CL+1)
 17774                              <1> 	;
 17775                              <1> 	;	NOTE: counter value, for example: even and odd numbers
 17776                              <1> 	;	      may be used for -audio- DMA buffer switch
 17777                              <1> 	;	      within double buffer method, etc.
 17778                              <1> 	;
 17779                              <1> 	;	EDX = Signal return (Response) byte address
 17780                              <1> 	;	       		  - or -
 17781                              <1> 	;	      Interrupt/Callback service/routine address
 17782                              <1> 	;
 17783                              <1> 	;	      (virtual address in user's memory space)
 17784                              <1> 	;
 17785                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
 17786                              <1> 	;	CF = 0 & EAX = 0 -> Successful setting
 17787                              <1> 	;	CF = 1 & EAX > 0 -> IRQ is prohibited or locked
 17788                              <1> 	;			by another process
 17789                              <1> 	;		 eax = ERR_PERM_DENIED -> prohibited or locked
 17790                              <1> 	;		 eax = ERR_INV_PARAMETER -> 
 17791                              <1> 	;		       invalid parameter/option or bad address
 17792                              <1> 	;
 17793                              <1> 	;	NOTE: Timer callbacks are set by using 'systimer'
 17794                              <1> 	;	      system call (IRQ 0, PIT and IRQ 8, RTC)
 17795                              <1> 	;
 17796                              <1> 	;	      Direct keyboard access is performed by using
 17797                              <1> 	;	      Keyboard Interrupt (INT 32h)
 17798                              <1> 	;
 17799                              <1> 	;	      It is prohibited here because:
 17800                              <1> 	;		1) Signal Response Byte method has not advantage
 17801                              <1> 	;		   against INT 32h, function AH = 1. Also,
 17802                              <1> 	;		   keyboard service interrupt will return with
 17803                              <1> 	;		   ascii and scan codes (AL, AH) while
 17804                              <1> 	;		   SRB method has only 1 byte space for ascii code
 17805                              <1> 	;		   or scan code. One byte signal response is used
 17806                              <1> 	;		   for ensuring very simple and very fast
 17807                              <1> 	;		   virtual to physical memory address conversion
 17808                              <1> 	;		   without any memory page crossover risk.
 17809                              <1> 	;		   (Otherwise double page conversion or word
 17810                              <1> 	;		   alignment would be needed.)
 17811                              <1> 	;		2) Badly written user code (callback code)
 17812                              <1> 	;		   can prevent keyboard and timesharing functions
 17813                              <1> 	;		   of the operating system via continuous and long
 17814                              <1> 	;		   keyboard event handling by callback service.
 17815                              <1> 	;		   (It can cause to lose immediate keystroke
 17816                              <1> 	;		   response from hardware to user.)
 17817                              <1> 	;		3) If user will check any keyboard events, 'getkey'
 17818                              <1> 	;		   (or 'getchar') must have more priority than other
 17819                              <1> 	;		   (video etc.) events because only control ability
 17820                              <1> 	;		   on a procedural infinite loop is a keyboard or
 17821                              <1> 	;		   mouse event. So user can use keyboard function
 17822                              <1> 	;		   at the end or at the beginning of a loop.
 17823                              <1> 	;		   In this case, INT 32h is used for that purpose
 17824                              <1> 	;		   and timer interrupt etc. callbacks can be used
 17825                              <1> 	;		   for dynamic and synchronized data refresh/transfer
 17826                              <1> 	;		   while cpu is in a static loop (without polling).
 17827                              <1> 	;		   Keyboard Int callback is not more useful because
 17828                              <1> 	;		   already a manual check (a key is pressed or not)
 17829                              <1> 	;		   can be performed (via INT 32h, AH = 1) efficiently
 17830                              <1> 	;		   in a loop to prevent a locked infinitive loop.
 17831                              <1> 	;
 17832                              <1> 	;	    Disk IRQs (6,14,15) have been phohibited from ring 3
 17833                              <1> 	;	    callback because, disk operations (file system services
 17834                              <1> 	;	    etc.) are independent from user program, for fast disk r/w.
 17835                              <1> 	;	    They are not more useful at ring 3 while they are in use
 17836                              <1> 	;	    by standard diskio functions which are mandatory part of
 17837                              <1> 	;	    (monolithic) OS kernel and mainprog command interpreter.
 17838                              <1> 	;	    INT 33h diskio functions are enough for user level disk
 17839                              <1> 	;	    r/w.
 17840                              <1> 	;
 17841                              <1> 	; TRDOS 386 - IRQ CALLBACK structures (parameters):
 17842                              <1> 	;
 17843                              <1> 	;	   [u.irqlock] = 1 word, IRQ flags (0-15) that indicates
 17844                              <1> 	;			which IRQs are locked by (that) user.
 17845                              <1> 	;		        Lock and unlock (by user) will change
 17846                              <1> 	;			these flags or 'terminate process' (sysexit)
 17847                              <1> 	;			will clear these flags and unlock those IRQs.
 17848                              <1> 	;
 17849                              <1> 	;		   	Bit 0 is for IRQ 0 and Bit 15 is for IRQ 15
 17850                              <1> 	;
 17851                              <1> 	;	   IRQ(x).owner	 : 1 byte, user, [u.uno], 0 = free (unlocked)
 17852                              <1> 	;
 17853                              <1> 	;	   IRQ(x).method : 1 byte for callback method & status
 17854                              <1> 	;			   0 = Signal Response Byte method
 17855                              <1> 	;			   1 = Callback service method
 17856                              <1> 	;			   >1 = invalid for current 'syscalback'.
 17857                              <1> 	;			or(+) 80h = IRQ is in use by system (ring 0)
 17858                              <1> 	;			            function (audio etc.) or
 17859                              <1> 	;			   	    a device driver.
 17860                              <1> 	;			(system function will ignore the lock/owner)
 17861                              <1> 	;
 17862                              <1> 	;	   IRQ(x).srb	: 1 byte, Signal Return/Response byte value
 17863                              <1> 	;			  (a fixed value by user or a counter value
 17864                              <1> 	;			 from 0 to 255, which is increased by every
 17865                              <1> 	;			 interrupt just before putting it into
 17866                              <1> 	;			 the Signal Response byte address
 17867                              <1> 	;			 (This is not used in callback serv method)
 17868                              <1> 	;
 17869                              <1> 	;	   IRQ(x).addr	: 1 dword
 17870                              <1> 	;			  Signal Response Byte address (physical)
 17871                              <1> 	;			  		-or-
 17872                              <1> 	;			  Callback service address (virtual)
 17873                              <1> 	;
 17874                              <1> 	;	   IRQ(x).dev	: 1 byte

 17876                              <1> 	;			  		-or-

 17880                              <1> 	;
 17881                              <1> 	;
 17882                              <1> 	;	NOTE: If user's process/program calls the kernel (INT 40h)
 17883                              <1> 	;	      while it is already running in a (ring 3) callback
 17884                              <1> 	;	      service, kernel will force (convert) system call to
 17885                              <1> 	;	      'sysrele' (sys release). So, this feature provides
 17886                              <1> 	;	      easy and simple usage of callback services without
 17887                              <1> 	;	      falling into deepless <please 'callback me' then
 17888                              <1> 	;	      let me 'callback you'> cycles! (User must return
 17889                              <1> 	;	      from callback service by using 'sysrele' system
 17890                              <1> 	;	      call, without a significant delay. Otherwise user
 17891                              <1> 	;	      process/program may be late to catch the next event
 17892                              <1> 	;	      within same callback purpose.

 18161                              <1> 	; 15/07/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.1.0
 18162                              <1> 	; 12/07/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.11

 18164                              <1> 	;	Explicit CHDIR Re-validation

 18213                              <1> syschmod: ; Get & Change File (or Directory) Attributes
 18214                              <1> 	; 02/01/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.10 (v2.1)
 18215                              <1> 	; 22/09/2025
 18216                              <1> 	; 26/09/2024 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.9
 18217                              <1> 	; 23/07/2022 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.5
 18218                              <1> 	; 19/01/2021
 18219                              <1> 	; 30/12/2017 (TRDOS 386 = TRDOS v2.0)
 18220                              <1> 	;
 18221                              <1>         ; INPUT ->
 18222                              <1>         ;          EBX = File/Directory (ASCIIZ) name address
 18223                              <1> 	;	    CL = New attributes (if CL < 40h)
 18224                              <1> 	;	    CL >= 40h -> Get File Attributes
 18225                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
 18226                              <1> 	;          cf = 0 -> EAX = File attributes (in AL)
 18227                              <1> 	;          cf = 1 -> Error code in AL
 18228                              <1> 	;
 18229                              <1> 	; Modified Registers: EAX (at the return of system call)
 18230                              <1> 	;
 18231                              <1> 	; MSDOS File Attributes:    (bit value of attrib byte)
 18232                              <1> 	;	ATTR_READ_ONLY	=	01h  (bit 0, 'R')
 18233                              <1> 	;	ATTR_HIDDEN	=	02h  (bit 1, 'H')
 18234                              <1> 	;	ATTR_SYSTEM	=	04h  (bit 2, 'S')
 18235                              <1> 	;	ATTR_VOLUME_ID	=	08h  (bit 3)
 18236                              <1> 	;	ATTR_DIRECTORY	=	10h  (bit 4)
 18237                              <1> 	;	ATTR_ARCHIVE	=	20h  (bit 5, 'A')
 18238                              <1> 	;	ATTR_LONG_NAME	=	ATTR_READONLY |
 18239                              <1> 	;				ATTR_HIDDEN |
 18240                              <1> 	;				ATTR_SYSTEM |
 18241                              <1> 	;				ATTR_VOLUME_ID
 18242                              <1> 	;	The upper two bits of attributes must be 0.

 18553                              <1> systime: ; Get System Date&Time
 18554                              <1> 	; 15/07/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.1.0
 18555                              <1> 	; 16/05/2026
 18556                              <1> 	; 15/05/2026
 18557                              <1> 	; 03/05/2026
 18558                              <1> 	; 01/05/2026 - TRDOS 386 v2.0.11
 18559                              <1> 	; 30/12/2017 (TRDOS 386 = TRDOS v2.0)
 18560                              <1> 	;
 18561                              <1>         ; INPUT -> BL =
 18562                              <1> 	;	    0 = Get Date&Time in Unix/Epoch format
 18563                              <1> 	;	    1 = Get Time in MSDOS format
 18564                              <1> 	;	    2 = Get Date in MSDOS format (1980->1980)
 18565                              <1> 	;	    3 = Get Date&Time in MSDOS format (1980->1980)
 18566                              <1> 	;	01/05/2026
 18567                              <1> 	;	    4 = Get/Return System Timer Ticks (18.2 Hz)
 18568                              <1> 	;		Note: If the system timer frequency is 100 Hz
 18569                              <1> 	;	             (18.2 Hz for the current kernel version),
 18570                              <1> 	; 		     the carry flag will be set on return.
 18571                              <1> 	;		-However, even if the system is running at 100 Hz,
 18572                              <1> 	;		 the number of ticks converted to 18.2 Hz will
 18573                              <1>         ;		 be returned-
 18574                              <1> 	;		100Hz to 18.2Hz conversion: int(timerticks*182/1000)
 18575                              <1> 	;	    5 = Get/Return System Timer Ticks (100 Hz)
 18576                              <1> 	;		Note: carry flag will be set at return
 18577                              <1> 	;		      if system timer frequency is NOT 100 Hz
 18578                              <1> 	;		(it is 18.2 Hz for current kernel version)
 18579                              <1> 	;		-However, even if the system is running at 18.2 Hz,
 18580                              <1> 	;		 the number of ticks converted to 100 Hz will
 18581                              <1>         ;		 be returned-
 18582                              <1> 	;		18.2Hz to 100Hz conversion: int(timerticks*1000/182)
 18583                              <1> 	;	    6 = Get Date&Time in MSDOS packed (direntry) format
 18584                              <1> 	;		(1980->0)
 18585                              <1> 	;	16/05/2026
 18586                              <1> 	;	    7 = Get Timer Ticks OVERFLOW Status
 18587                              <1> 	; 	    8 = Get Day Of The Week
 18588                              <1> 	;
 18589                              <1> 	;	    9 & other values (>9) =
 18590                              <1> 	;		System timer ticks will be returned
 18591                              <1> 	;		in EAX and Carry Flag will be set.
 18592                              <1> 	; OUTPUT ->
 18593                              <1> 	;	For BL input = 3
 18594                              <1> 	;          EAX = Current Time (RTC)
 18595                              <1> 	;		AL = Second (DL in MSDOS)
 18596                              <1> 	;		AH = Minute (CL in MSDOS)
 18597                              <1> 	;	   	HW of EAX = Hour (CH in MSDOS)
 18598                              <1> 	;	   EDX = Current System Date (RTC)
 18599                              <1> 	;		DL = Day (DL in MSDOS)
